equivalents.note: Expands stage 6 (the auxiliaries of nididhyāsana: savikalpa and nirvikalpa samādhi).
Śaṅkara-attributed fifteen limbs of 'rāja-yoga' re-described as knowledge; a parallel Advaita path.
Vidyāraṇya's Jīvanmuktiviveka uses the seven bhūmikās to grade Advaita knowers (stages 4-7 ~ this map's 7-9).
Dvaita also teaches śravaṇa-manana-nididhyāsana leading to aparokṣa-jñāna, but of the Lord as other than the self; Dvaita rejects the identity this map's stage 7 names.

tradition_objection: Advaita holds that liberation is not produced by any stage: Brahman is ever-attained and knowledge only removes ignorance. The stages are for removing obstacles according to the student's fitness (adhikāra); for the best student a single hearing of the great sentence is enough (BSBh 4.1.2). The Vivaraṇa school makes hearing the principal means and reflection and contemplation its auxiliaries; the Bhāmatī school gives contemplation (prasaṅkhyāna) a larger role.
notes: Uses existing U03/U13 teachings. Stage 9 (the liberated one's life) is placed before videhamukti because it belongs to the living knower.

stages.band_note: B0 by what it names; Dōgen denies that it precedes the others (way-ring).

stages.description: Practice is practice-in-realization (shō-jō no shu): the beginner's wholehearted practice of the way is the whole of original realization; just sit, thinking not-thinking.
stages.band_note: B6 in Dōgen's own terms ('practice on top of realization'), not as a preparatory stage (B2-B4); it is listed before awakening because Dōgen lists it so.

stages.name: bodai 菩提
stages.description: 'That the myriad things come forward and verify the self is awakening'; awakening is like the moon in water — the moon does not get wet, the water is not broken.
stages.band_note: Banded B5 by what it names; for Dōgen it is not after practice.

stages.name: nehan 涅槃
stages.description: The fourth phase of the ring, returning without gap to arousing the mind; 'when the myriad dharmas are without self there is no delusion, no awakening, no buddhas, no beings'.

equivalents.note: Both are Zen maps, but Dōgen rejects treating practice as a means to a later awakening, which the pictures' sequence suggests.
Jinul puts cultivation after awakening; Dōgen makes them one — 'practice on top of realization' is close to Jinul's order, but Dōgen denies any sequence.
Both traditions deny that practice produces what is already complete ('the Way is fundamentally complete'; the all-creating king has nothing to do).

tradition_objection: Dōgen denies that this is a ladder: 'to think practice and realization are not one is a non-Buddhist view'; the four phases form a ring without the slightest gap, and the Way 'is fundamentally complete — why depend on practice and realization?', yet 'if there is the slightest gap, heaven and earth are far apart'. The bands therefore do not describe an order of attainment; they only record which band each named phase would occupy on other maps.
notes: The four phases are from the Gyōji fascicle (text not available locally; moderate confidence on wording). Bands are deliberately non-monotonic (B0, B6, B5, B7) to show that Dōgen places 'practice' where other maps place post-awakening cultivation.

name: The four visions of Direct Crossing (thod rgal gyi snang ba bzhi)

stages.name: chos nyid mngon sum

stages.band_note: B5 as the first direct manifestation; the recognition of awareness on which it rests (cutting through) is itself B5 on pth:yeshe-lama-path.

stages.name: nyams gong 'phel
stages.description: The visionary display increases and develops.

stages.name: rig pa tshad phebs
stages.description: Awareness reaches its full extent; the display is complete.

stages.name: chos nyid zad pa
stages.description: All appearances dissolve into dharmatā; the texts speak of the body of light (rainbow body) as its sign.

equivalents.note: The four visions are the direct-crossing stage of Jigme Lingpa's Yeshe Lama map (U45).
Both describe the ripening of the recognition of mind's nature to its exhaustion/non-meditation; neither tradition treats them as identical systems.
Both are completion-level practices in which appearances of light arise and are recognized as the mind's own display; methods and views differ.

tradition_objection: Dzogchen holds that awareness is primordially complete and is not produced by stages: the Kunjed Gyalpo says there is nothing to be done, no view to meditate and no path to traverse, and 'whatever is meditated is my sickness'; the four visions are the self-display of spontaneous presence, not a ladder of attainment. Direct crossing is taught only to those stable in cutting through.
notes: RESTRICTED: direct crossing (thod rgal) is a restricted practice; only the names of the four visions and the texts' own framing are recorded — no postures, gazes, lamps or other method details. Stage names are the standard ones (moderate-to-high confidence); precise textual loci in the Seventeen Tantras are not given (chapter-level refs only).

stages.name: undistracted single mind in phenomena (shi yixin)
undistracted single mind in principle (li yixin)
birth, grade according to the depth of holding the name

notes: Stages 4–5 combine Ouyi with Zhuhong's two kinds of single mind (recalled).

name: The five paths (pañca-mārga): accumulation, preparation, seeing, cultivation, no-more-learning

stages.name: saṃbhāra-mārga
stages.description: Entered with the uncontrived mind of awakening (or, for the lesser vehicles, renunciation); accumulation of merit and wisdom by hearing, reflection, ethics and calm abiding.
stages.band_note: B2 as accumulation and training; its entry (bodhicitta) is B0 and its greater level includes calm abiding (B3-B4).

stages.name: prayoga-mārga
stages.description: Four stages — heat, peak, patience, supreme mundane quality — in which, by insight joined to calm, the grasped and then the grasper are seen as empty/mind-only; 'the aids to penetration'.
stages.band_note: B4: insight that still has a conceptual object (this unit's rule); the direct seeing comes at the next path.

stages.name: darśana-mārga
stages.description: The first direct, non-conceptual seeing of reality: the dharmadhātu directly perceived, free of duality; sixteen moments (eight acceptances and eight knowledges) regarding the four truths; the first bodhisattva ground.

stages.name: bhāvanā-mārga
stages.description: The remaining grounds (2-10): non-conceptual knowledge purifying the buddha-qualities and subsequent knowledge maturing beings, until the diamond-like concentration.

stages.name: aśaikṣa-mārga / niṣṭhā-mārga
stages.description: The final transformation of the basis, stainless of all obscurations: buddhahood (for the lesser vehicles, arhatship); the dharma-body.

stages.name: buddha-karma
stages.gloss: the activity of the buddhas (in Gampopa's sequence)
stages.description: The buddhas' activity benefits beings spontaneously and without conceptual thought, like the sun shining or a wish-fulfilling jewel; it is effortless and uninterrupted.
stages.band_note: Not one of the five paths; added from Gampopa's Jewel Ornament (and the Ratnagotravibhāga), which follow the paths with buddhahood and its activity.

equivalents.note: Xuanzang's five stages of the path to cognition-only (資糧, 加行, 通達, 修習, 究竟) are the five paths.
The Sarvāstivāda path has the same preparatory aids (heat, peak, patience, supreme mundane) and the paths of seeing, cultivation and no-more-learning.
Path of seeing = first ground; path of cultivation = grounds 2-10; no-more-learning = buddhahood.
In the Abhidharma and Mahāyāna presentations stream-entry is on the path of seeing and arhatship at no-more-learning.
Padampa Sangye arranges Pacification along these five paths.
Kagyu masters correlate the four yogas with the five paths in differing ways (Moonbeams).

notes: Pan-Mahāyāna frame (Yogācāra sources, Abhisamayālaṃkāra, Tibetan lamrim and grounds-and-paths literature; also applied to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas). Stage 6 is outside the five and marked as such.

name: The fivefold Mahāmudrā
notes: The five are practised together in each session, not as successive stages; the bands say what kind of practice each element is, not a sequence. Dedication is left unbanded.

name: The four orders of life in sequence (Manu)

stages.name: upanayana
stages.description: Entry into Vedic study with the Sāvitrī (MDh 2.36, 2.169–171).

stages.name: brahmacarya
stages.description: Study of the Veda in the teacher's house, chastity, service, sense-restraint (MDh 2; 3.1–2).

stages.name: gārhasthya
stages.description: Marriage, the five great sacrifices, the debts to gods, seers and ancestors, livelihood by one's dharma (MDh 3–5).

stages.name: vānaprasthya
stages.description: Withdrawal to the forest with austerities, study of the Upaniṣads and daily rites (MDh 6.1–32).

stages.name: saṃnyāsa / parivrājya
stages.description: Depositing the fires in oneself, wandering alone, breath-control, fixation, withdrawal and meditation, seeing the self in all (MDh 6.33–85).

stages.name: brahmaṇy avasthāna
stages.description: Freed from all pairs of opposites, he abides in Brahman; one with right vision is not bound by actions (MDh 6.74, 6.81).

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer claims (logged). Other texts allow the orders as options or recognize only the householder (dsp:asrama-vikalpa-samuccaya-badha).

name: The four dharmas of Gampopa

stages.name: blo chos su 'gro ba
stages.gloss: the mind turns to the Dharma
stages.description: renunciation through the four thoughts

stages.name: chos lam du 'gro ba
stages.description: refuge, love, compassion and bodhicitta make practice a real path

stages.name: lam 'khrul pa sel ba
stages.description: meditation (śamatha–vipaśyanā) and insight into emptiness dispel confusion

stages.name: 'khrul pa ye shes su 'char ba
stages.description: Mahāmudrā realization: confusion itself is recognized as wisdom

notes: The glosses of each line follow the common Kagyu explanation (from memory); the four lines are a summary rather than a strict ladder.

name: The four stages of awakening and the eight noble persons

stages.name: sotāpattiyaṅga
stages.description: Association with good persons, hearing the true Dhamma, wise attention, practice in accordance with the Dhamma.

stages.name: sotāpatti-magga (saddhānusārī / dhammānusārī)
stages.description: The path moment: the Dhamma-eye arises — 'whatever is subject to arising is subject to cessation'.

stages.name: sotāpanna
stages.description: By the destruction of three fetters (personality view, doubt, clinging to rules and observances): not subject to the lower realms, fixed in destiny, bound for awakening; confirmed confidence in the three jewels and the virtues dear to the noble ones ('the mirror of the Dhamma').

stages.name: sakadāgāmi-magga
stages.description: The second path.

stages.name: sakadāgāmī
stages.description: Three fetters destroyed and lust, hate and delusion weakened: returns to this world once and makes an end of suffering.

stages.name: anāgāmi-magga
stages.description: The third path, abandoning the five lower fetters (with sensual desire and ill will), for instance by seeing the aggregates in a jhāna as impermanent and turning to the deathless.

stages.name: anāgāmī
stages.description: The five lower fetters destroyed: spontaneously reborn (in the Pure Abodes), attaining final nibbāna there without returning from that world.

stages.name: arahatta-magga
stages.description: The fourth path, abandoning the five higher fetters (lust for form and the formless, conceit, restlessness, ignorance).

stages.name: arahant
stages.description: By the destruction of the effluents, having realized for himself here and now the effluent-free freedom of mind and freedom by wisdom: 'birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, done is what was to be done'.

equivalents.note: Sarvāstivāda has the same four fruits and eight persons, with a different account of the path of seeing (fifteen/sixteen moments).
Stream-entry corresponds to the path of seeing, the higher paths to the path of cultivation, arahantship to no-more-learning, in the Abhidharma and Mahāyāna presentations.
Stream-entry and Jain right view are both the first irreversible seeing that bounds the remaining births; the not-self teaching and the Jain soul-doctrine are not reconciled by this.

notes: Stage 1 (factors for stream-entry) is added as the entry named in SN 55.5. The canonical eight persons are AN 8.59 (Pali root checked locally); DN 16 2.7 gives the defining formulas (checked locally). Lay followers attain all three lower fruits in DN 16.

name: Torrent, river, ocean (Tilopa's Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā)

stages.name: gcong rong chu
stages.description: Beginning practice, turbulent.

stages.name: chu bo gang+gA
stages.description: Middle practice, steady.

stages.name: chu bran ma bu phrad
stages.gloss: river meeting the ocean, mother and child
stages.description: Final realization.

notes: Correspondence with the later four yogas of mahāmudrā (pth:mahamudra-four-yogas) is not stated by Tilopa.

name: The seven means of the 'yoga of the pot' (ghaṭastha-yoga) in the Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā

stages.name: śodhana through ṣaṭkarma
stages.description: Dhauti, vasti, neti, laulikī, trāṭaka and kapālabhāti cleanse the body (the unbaked pot to be fired in the fire of yoga).
stages.band_note: B1 by the text's own word śodhana (purification) — bodily, not ethical, purification; some acts of this chapter are restricted (summary only).

stages.name: dṛḍhatā through āsana
stages.description: Of the eighty-four lakh postures taught by Śiva, thirty-two are described.

stages.name: sthiratā through mudrā
stages.description: Twenty-five mudrās (mahāmudrā, bandhas, khecarī, viparītakaraṇī, śakticālana and others).
stages.band_note: Several of these seals are restricted practices (khecarī, vajroṇī): summary only.

stages.name: dhairya through pratyāhāra
stages.description: Wherever the fickle mind wanders, it is drawn back and brought under the control of the self.

stages.name: lāghava through prāṇāyāma
stages.description: After place, time, moderate diet and purification of the channels, eight kinds of retention (kumbhaka) are taught.
stages.band_note: Banded B2 by kind (breath discipline) although the text places it after withdrawal; the order is the Gheraṇḍa's own and is kept.

stages.name: pratyakṣa through dhyāna
stages.gloss: direct perception (of the self) through meditation
stages.description: Meditation is threefold — gross (on a form), of light, and subtle (on bindu/kuṇḍalinī) — and yields 'direct perception in the self'.
stages.band_note: Banded by the fruit the text names (pratyakṣam ātmani, direct perception of the self, B5); the practice itself — visualized form, light, bindu — is absorption with support (B4).

stages.name: nirliptatva through samādhi
stages.description: Samādhi, obtained by the guru's grace, is separating the mind from the body and uniting it with the supreme self: 'I am Brahman'; 'through samādhi, untaintedness, and liberation without doubt'.

equivalents.note: Stage 7 is expanded into six kinds of samādhi in GhS 7.
Four limb-names shared (āsana, pratyāhāra, prāṇāyāma, dhyāna, samādhi); yama/niyama replaced by bodily cleansing; mudrā added; order of prāṇāyāma and pratyāhāra reversed.

notes: Verified locally against the DCS text of the Gheraṇḍasaṃhitā (1.10-11: śodhanaṃ dṛḍhatā caiva sthairyaṃ dhairyaṃ ca lāghavam / pratyakṣaṃ ca nirliptaṃ ca …; ṣaṭkarmaṇā śodhanaṃ … samādhinā nirliptaṃ ca muktir eva na saṃśayaḥ). The chapter order of the text follows the seven means.

name: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā: the six samādhis (parallel routes)

stages.name: bhakti-yoga samādhi
stages.gloss: by devotion to the chosen deity

stages.name: manomūrcchā samādhi
stages.gloss: by the swoon of the mind

notes: NOT a sequence: six alternative routes to the one samādhi that the GS calls rājayoga and 'the mark of liberation' (7.17). 'order' is the text's order of exposition only. All banded B4 (absorption), with the text's claim of liberation (B7) noted. Verse refs of 7.7–16 recalled from structure.

name: The ascent in yoga of BhG ch. 6

stages.name: ārurukṣu
stages.description: For the sage wishing to ascend to yoga, action is the means (6.3).

stages.name: yogārūḍha
stages.description: When attached neither to objects nor to actions and having renounced all intentions, one has ascended; quiescence is then the means (6.2–4).

stages.name: dhyāna practice
stages.description: Seated firmly, erect, gaze controlled, the mind is made one-pointed, stilled by degrees and brought back whenever it wanders; it becomes steady like a lamp in a windless place (6.10–26).

stages.name: brahma-saṃsparśa
stages.description: The calm yogin attains the endless happiness of contact with Brahman and sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self (6.27–29).

stages.name: seeing the Lord everywhere
stages.description: He sees the Lord everywhere and everything in him, worships him abiding in all beings, and regards others' pleasure and pain as his own (6.30–32).

stages.name: peace culminating in nirvāṇa
stages.description: The yogin attains the peace that culminates in nirvāṇa and abides in the Lord (6.15); of all yogins the one who worships him with faith is the most yoked (6.47).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch04-06): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; corrections logged in interpretation_log.jsonl.

notes: If the yogin falls short, the effort is carried into a later birth (6.40–45).
alt_notes: Merged from extractor A (8 stages, this id) and extractor B (pth:bhagavad-gita-aruruksu-yogarudha: ārurukṣu → yogārūḍha → the highest peace). Only stages 1–2 are given by the text as an explicit sequence (6.3); stages 3–7 follow the chapter's order of description, not a numbered sequence (B recorded those states as phenomenology instead), and stage 8 is the chapter's own statement of the result. The chapter also says the ascent may span many births (6.41–45) and that of all yogins the faithful worshipper of the Lord is the most yoked (6.47). Band assignments are interpretive (interpretation layer).

name: The graded devotional practices of BhG 12.8–12

stages.name: karmaphala-tyāga
stages.gloss: relinquishing the fruit of all actions
stages.description: If one cannot do even the Lord's work, then, taking refuge in his yoga and self-controlled, give up the fruit of all actions (12.11).

stages.name: mat-karma-parama
stages.gloss: being intent on the Lord's work
stages.description: If one cannot practise, be intent on doing actions for the Lord's sake; even so one attains perfection (12.10).

stages.name: abhyāsa-yoga
stages.description: If one cannot fix the mind steadily, seek to reach the Lord by the yoga of practice (12.9).

stages.name: fixing mind and intellect on the Lord
stages.description: Fix your mind on the Lord alone and rest your intellect in him (12.8).

stages.name: dwelling in the Lord
stages.description: Thereafter you will dwell in him (12.8).

checks.note: Fidelity checker F (bhagavad-gita ch10-12): this unit's contribution checked against the Sanskrit of the cited verses; corrections logged in interpretation_log.jsonl.

notes: The text presents the steps from the highest downward as alternatives by capacity; they are listed here from the most accessible upward. 12.12 gives a different ranking (practice < knowledge < meditation < relinquishing the fruit, from which peace follows); commentators reconcile the two differently.
alt_notes: The text states the four instructions from the highest downward (12.8, then 'if you cannot …' 12.9, 12.10, 12.11), each for one unable to do the previous; they are listed here upward from the most accessible, as the conditional sequence implies. 12.12 then ranks knowledge above practice, meditation above knowledge and relinquishing the fruit of actions above meditation, with peace following immediately on relinquishment — an order that does not coincide with 12.8–11, where relinquishment is the step for one unable to do the others; Śaṅkara reads 12.12 as praise (stuti) of relinquishment (recalled; see the notes of teaching 12.12), and the commentators take the ranking variously. Bands are interpretive and left to the interpretation layer.

name: From one's own work to entering the Lord (BhG 18.45–56)

stages.name: svakarma as worship
stages.gloss: worshipping the Lord by one's own work
stages.description: Each devoted to his own work attains perfection by worshipping with it him from whom beings arise (18.45–46).

stages.name: naiṣkarmya-siddhi
stages.gloss: the perfection of freedom from action
stages.description: With intellect unattached everywhere, self-conquered, free of longing, one attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action (18.49).

stages.name: dhyāna-yoga and fitness for Brahman
stages.description: With purified intellect, restraint, solitude, light food, controlled speech, body and mind, constant meditation, dispassion, and the giving up of ego, force, pride, desire, anger and possession, one becomes fit for becoming Brahman (18.50–53).

stages.name: brahmabhūta
stages.description: Having become Brahman, serene, one neither grieves nor desires and is the same to all beings (18.54).

stages.name: parā bhakti
stages.description: He attains supreme devotion to the Lord, and by devotion knows him in truth (18.54–55).

stages.name: entering the Lord; the eternal abode
stages.description: Knowing him in truth he enters him; even while doing all actions, taking refuge in him, by his grace he attains the eternal, imperishable abode (18.55–56).

notes: Stage order is the text's; the bands are the interpretation layer. Commentators differ on whether knowledge (Advaita) or devotion (Vaiṣṇava) is the final stage — see dsp:gita-primary-teaching.

name: The six-limbed yoga of the Gorakṣaśataka

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: Siddhāsana and padmāsana, the two pre-eminent of the eighty-four; posture destroys disease (GŚ 5–9, 54).

stages.name: prāṇasaṃyāma
stages.description: Alternate breathing through moon and sun with the five seals; it burns sin; signs of sweat, trembling, rising (GŚ 32–53).

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: The sun draws in the moon's nectar; withdrawal removes mental disturbance (GŚ 54–66).

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Holding the mind on the five elements in heart, throat, palate, brows and brahmarandhra (GŚ 67–75).

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Meditation with qualities on the centres and without qualities on Śiva and the all-pervading self (GŚ 76–93).

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: The samarasa oneness when breath is exhausted and mind dissolved; beyond time and karma; non-duality in the supreme state like milk in milk (GŚ 94–101).

name: The gradual training (anupubbasikkhā) of the Sāmaññaphala and related suttas

stages.name: tathāgatuppāda, dhammassavana
stages.gloss: a Tathāgata arises; hearing the Dhamma
stages.description: A Tathāgata arises and teaches; a householder hears the Dhamma and gains faith.

stages.name: pabbajjā
stages.description: Seeing the household life as crowded, he goes forth into homelessness.

stages.name: sīla
stages.description: Restraint by the Pātimokkha and the short, middle and long sections on virtue; blameless happiness.

stages.name: indriyasaṃvara
stages.description: Not grasping at signs and features of sense objects.

stages.name: satisampajañña
stages.description: Full awareness in all activities.

stages.name: santuṭṭhi
stages.description: Content with robes and alms, like a bird with its wings.

stages.name: nīvaraṇappahāna
stages.description: In a secluded place, mindfulness established, he cleanses the mind of the five hindrances; gladness and joy arise.

stages.name: cattāri jhānāni
stages.description: The four absorptions with their similes of bodily pervasion.

stages.name: ñāṇadassana
stages.description: Directing the concentrated mind to see the body as material and consciousness as bound up with it.

stages.name: abhiññā
stages.gloss: mind-made body and the direct knowledges
stages.description: Mind-made body, psychic powers, divine ear, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of past lives, divine eye.

stages.name: āsavakkhayañāṇa
stages.gloss: knowledge of the destruction of the effluents
stages.description: Knowing the four truths and the effluents as they are; liberation and the knowledge 'birth is ended'.

summary: The step-by-step path from hearing the Dhamma to the destruction of the effluents, given in DN 2 and repeated with variations in DN 1–13, MN 27, MN 38, MN 39, MN 51, MN 107 and MN 125.
notes: Band B4 for the direct knowledges is an interpretation: the texts present them as attainments of the concentrated mind before the final knowledge, not as insight.

name: The six-limbed service of the Guhyasamāja (ch. 18)

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: The ten senses resting in their own places; blessed by all mantras.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: The five objects of desire as the five buddhas, fivefold; the five superknowledges.

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: The five-gnosis breath as a jewel at the nose tip; blessed by bodhisattvas.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Mantra in the heart in the drop of life-wind; the five signs; Vajrasattva enters.

stages.name: anusmṛti
stages.description: Recollecting the visualized form, an appearance arises; a halo of light.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Sudden arising of gnosis; free of obscurations.

notes: Verse numbers are the unit's count in Bhattacharya's e-text; bands are interpretive. U51 owns the Kālacakra version (pth:kalacakra-six-branches), which has the same order of limbs.

name: The Hakuin-line kōan curriculum

stages.name: shokan (first barrier): mu or the sound of one hand
stages.description: Great doubt on an initial kōan leading to kenshō.

stages.name: hosshin kōan
stages.description: Clarifying the undifferentiated.

stages.name: kikan kōan
stages.description: Function within differentiation.

stages.name: gonsen kōan
stages.description: Penetrating the ancients' words.

stages.name: goi
stages.description: The Caodong five ranks studied as kōans.

stages.name: jūjūkinkai
stages.description: The precepts studied as kōans.

name: Haribhadra's eight views of yoga (yoga-dṛṣṭi)

stages.name: mitrā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: friendly — like straw-fire spark; limb: yama; fault removed: fatigue (kheda); quality: non-aversion (adveṣa)
stages.description: The dim first view: restraints present as wish, no weariness in worship, no aversion; the 'seeds of yoga' (devotion to the Jina, service of teachers, disgust with existence) are sown.
stages.band_note: B0 as the sowing of the seeds of yoga; Haribhadra pairs it with yama (B1).

stages.name: tārā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: star-like — like cow-dung fire; limb: niyama; fault removed: anxiety (udvega); quality: desire to know (jijñāsā)
stages.description: Observances appear; no anxiety in doing good; desire to know the truth.

stages.name: balā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: strong — like wood fire; limb: āsana; fault removed: distraction (kṣepa); quality: desire to hear (śuśrūṣā)
stages.description: Posture steady, restlessness gone, longing to hear the truth.

stages.name: dīprā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: shining — like lamp; limb: prāṇāyāma; fault removed: interruption (utthāna); quality: hearing (śravaṇa)
stages.description: Breath-control in an inner sense (expelling outer states, taking in inner ones); the truth is heard, but the subtle knot is not yet broken.

stages.name: sthirā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: steady — like gem; limb: pratyāhāra; fault removed: error (bhrānti); quality: understanding (bodha)
stages.description: The knot is broken and right view arises; worldly doings look like children's houses of dust.
stages.band_note: B5 by the Jain criterion (right view, knot broken); Haribhadra's paired limb, pratyāhāra, would be B3 on the Pātañjala map — both recorded.

stages.name: kāntā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: lovely — like star; limb: dhāraṇā; fault removed: delight in other things (anyamud); quality: reflection (mīmāṃsā)
stages.description: Concentration firm; acting in the world with the mind fixed on dharma.

stages.name: prabhā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: radiant — like sun; limb: dhyāna; fault removed: affliction/disease (ruj); quality: practice (pratipatti)
stages.description: Meditation prevails with its happiness; activity free of attachment — what others call the peaceful flow and the way of Śiva.

stages.name: parā dṛṣṭi
stages.gloss: supreme — like moon; limb: samādhi; fault removed: attachment (āsaṅga); quality: right engagement (pravṛtti)
stages.description: Absorption free of attachment; beyond practices; omniscience; renouncing even yoga (yoga-saṃnyāsa), liberation.

sources.ref: 13-16 and the sections on each view

equivalents.note: Haribhadra pairs the views with Patañjali's limbs (YDS 16), reinterpreted inwardly; stated by the text itself.
The first four views lie within guṇasthāna 1 (ogha-dṛṣṭi); sthirā begins right view (4+); parā is kevala (13-14).
Haribhadra's four kinds of yogin grade the same practitioners by family and progress.

notes: The eight faults and eight qualities are given from memory of YDS 16 and its auto-commentary (moderate confidence on the exact pairing). Haribhadra addresses yogins of other schools too (YDS 129-134: the omniscient teachers of different schools are not really different), so the views are meant to be applicable across traditions. The first four views are unstable (they can fall back); the last four are stable.

name: Haribhadra's four kinds of yogins

stages.name: gotra-yogin
stages.description: Born in a family of yogins but without the qualities; not fit for instruction.

stages.name: kula-yogin
stages.description: Born with the dharma of yogins; fit for instruction.

stages.name: pravṛttacakra-yogin
stages.description: Has the desire- and practice-grades of restraint; the teaching is chiefly for him.

stages.name: niṣpanna-yogin
stages.description: Yoga completed; beyond instruction.

name: The four stages of yoga practice (ārambha, ghaṭa, paricaya, niṣpatti)

stages.name: ārambha
stages.description: With the channels purified, signs appear (lightness, radiance, sweat, trembling, hopping); in the Haṭhayogapradīpikā the knot of Brahmā is pierced and the tinkling unstruck sound is heard with bliss from the void.
stages.band_note: B2 in the DYŚ/ŚS account (signs of breath-discipline); the HYP's nāda version already begins at B3 (so U28's pth:hyp-nada-four-stages).

stages.name: ghaṭa
stages.description: Prāṇa and apāna, nāda and bindu, the individual and the supreme self 'meet'; sense-withdrawal while established in retention; in the HYP the breath, made one, enters the middle and the knot of Viṣṇu is pierced (kettledrum sound).

stages.name: paricaya
stages.description: The breath enters suṣumnā unobstructed with the awakened kuṇḍalinī; the fivefold element-concentrations; in the HYP the breath reaches the great void, sound of a drum, natural bliss.

stages.name: niṣpatti
stages.description: Rājayoga: the seeds of karma are crossed and samādhi arises for the one liberated while living (ŚS); the knot of Rudra is pierced, flute and vīṇā sounds, the mind becomes one (HYP); the stage gives both enjoyment and liberation (DYŚ).

equivalents.note: The Haṭhayogapradīpikā's account of the same four stages through inner sound and the three knots.
The Śiva Saṃhitā's account of the same four stages.
The Yogatattva Upaniṣad's account of the same four stages.
Both describe the breath/kuṇḍalinī passing the knots or centres up the central channel.

notes: Umbrella map for the four avasthās 'in all yogas' (HYP 4.69; ŚS 3.31; DYŚ 9-10), first taught in the Amṛtasiddhi. The texts describe the stages chiefly through breath-retention and its signs; retention counts and durations are deliberately omitted (restricted). The existing text-specific maps (U28, U29, U04) are the detailed versions; this map aligns them.

name: Hemacandra's four kinds of mind and the no-mind state (Yogaśāstra 12)

stages.name: vikṣipta
stages.description: Restless.
stages.band_note: Starting condition, unbanded.

stages.name: yātāyāta
stages.description: Goes out and returns; has some bliss.

stages.name: śliṣṭa
stages.description: Steady and blissful.

stages.name: sulīna
stages.description: Very steady, with the highest bliss.

stages.name: unmanībhāva
stages.description: When the mind is left alone in indifference it becomes still of itself; in the no-mind state the self is realised and the yogin, like one freed of a load, experiences bliss.
stages.band_note: B5 by the text's claim that the self is realised here; low confidence on verse numbers.

equivalents.note: Graded minds/practitioners in the Yoga tradition; Vyāsa's five levels of mind (kṣipta … niruddha, YBh 1.1) are a closer analogue.

notes: Hemacandra introduces chapter 12 as the reality established by his own experience (12.1), after eleven chapters drawn from scripture. The four minds are also named in the Amanaska tradition of 'no-mind'; no borrowing claim is made here.

name: Haṭhapradīpikā: the four stages of nāda

stages.name: ārambha
stages.description: brahmagranthi pierced; bliss from the void; tinkling sounds; radiant, fragrant body

stages.name: ghaṭa
stages.description: breath united enters the middle; viṣṇugranthi pierced; kettledrum sound in the extreme void

stages.name: paricaya
stages.description: drum sound; breath in the great void, abode of powers; natural bliss

stages.name: niṣpatti
stages.description: rudragranthi pierced; flute and vīṇā; mind one — rājayoga; liberation while living

notes: The HYP's form of the four stages (pth:hatha-four-stages, U51) keyed to the knots and the inner sounds. Banding is an interpretation: ārambha as one-pointed absorption in sound (B3), ghaṭa and paricaya as absorption with support (B4), niṣpatti = rājayoga = jīvanmukti (B7). The text has no separate 'seeing' stage (B5/B6); do not force one.

name: Haṭhapradīpikā: the order of practice

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: the first limb of haṭha: steadiness, health, lightness

stages.name: kumbhaka
stages.description: breath-control after purification of the channels

stages.name: mudrā / karaṇa
stages.description: the ten mudrās that awaken kuṇḍalinī

stages.name: nādānusandhāna
stages.description: the chief of the layas

stages.name: rājayoga (samādhi)
stages.description: the mindless state; liberation while living

notes: The sequence HYP 1.56 states (āsana, kumbhaka, mudrā, nādānusandhāna), practised 'until the fruit, rājayoga' (1.67). The yamas/niyamas (B1) are not a separate limb in the HYP. Banding by U28.

name: Prajāpati's four instructions to Indra (ChU 8.7-12)
description: Four successive teachings over 32 + 32 + 32 + 5 = 101 years, each tested by Indra until the last.

stages.name: the person seen in the eye / the reflected body
stages.description: Taught first; Virocana stops here and teaches the asuras that the body is the self; Indra sees the flaw.

stages.name: the one who moves about in dreams
stages.description: Not harmed by the body's defects, but seems to suffer.

stages.name: the one fully asleep, serene, seeing no dream
stages.description: Then one does not know oneself or beings, 'gone to annihilation as it were'.

stages.name: the serene one who reaches the highest light
stages.gloss: the bodiless self in its own form
stages.description: The body is the mortal base of the immortal bodiless self; rising from it, reaching the highest light, it appears in its own form.

notes: Stages 2-3 are provisional teachings, not practices; no band assigned. Advaita reads the sequence as superimposition and retraction (U13).

checks.note: Located: ChU 8.7.3, 8.9.3, 8.10.3 (32 years each) and 8.11.3 (5 more years; 'ekaśataṃ ha vai varṣāṇi maghavān prajāpatau brahmacaryam uvāsa'). The four teachings are at 8.7.4, 8.10.1, 8.11.1 and 8.12. All 6 Upaniṣad refs cited in the entry are located in the prepared segments (ChU 8.7-12; ChU 8.7.4-8.9.1; ChU 8.10.1-4; ChU 8.11.1-3; ChU 8.12.1-6; ChU 8.7-8.12). It rests on 6 teaching(s) text-located in this sweep, and its wording matches those passages.

name: The ascent through virtuous and pure meditation

stages.name: ājñā-vicaya
stages.description: Virtuous meditation on the realities as taught.

stages.name: apāya-vicaya
stages.description: Virtuous meditation on the misery of wrong ways.

stages.name: vipāka-vicaya
stages.description: Virtuous meditation on karma's fruition.

stages.name: saṃsthāna-vicaya
stages.description: Virtuous meditation on the universe.

stages.name: pṛthaktva-vitarka-savīcāra
stages.description: Scripture-based meditation shifting among aspects (stages 8–11).

stages.name: ekatva-vitarka-avīcāra
stages.description: Fixed on one aspect; destroys the destructive karmas (stage 12).

stages.name: kevala-jñāna
stages.description: Omniscience arises (stage 13).

stages.name: sūkṣmakriyā-apratipāti
stages.description: The omniscient's subtle-activity meditation at life's end.

stages.name: vyuparatakriyā-anivarti
stages.description: All activity stopped (stage 14).

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: Release from all karma; the soul rises to the summit.

notes: The living omniscient's teaching activity (stage 13) could also be read as band B8.

name: The eleven stages of the householder (pratimā)

stages.name: darśana
stages.description: Right view purified, with the basic qualities.

stages.name: vrata
stages.description: The twelve lay vows without transgression.

stages.name: sāmāyika
stages.description: Regular equanimity practice.

stages.name: proṣadha
stages.description: Fasting and retreat on the parvan days.

stages.name: sacitta-tyāga
stages.description: Not eating uncooked, living vegetable food.

stages.name: rātribhukti-tyāga
stages.description: (Some texts: celibacy by day.)

stages.name: brahmacarya
stages.description: Complete sexual abstinence.

stages.name: ārambha-tyāga
stages.description: Ceasing business and household undertakings.

stages.name: parigraha-tyāga
stages.description: Relinquishing property.

stages.name: anumati-tyāga
stages.description: Not giving consent to household affairs.

stages.name: uddiṣṭa-tyāga
stages.gloss: not accepting food prepared for oneself
stages.description: Living almost as a monk (Digambara kṣullaka/ailaka).

notes: Śvetāmbara list differs (view, vow, sāmāyika, pauṣadha, kāyotsarga, celibacy, living food, undertakings, employing others, prepared food, living like a monk — recalled). Stages after right view are banded B6 (cultivation after seeing).

name: The four objects of meditation (piṇḍastha to rūpātīta)

stages.name: piṇḍastha
stages.description: Five visualised concentrations: earth, fire, wind, water, the essential.

stages.name: padastha
stages.description: Meditation on letters, 'arhaṃ' and the homage to the supreme beings.

stages.name: rūpastha
stages.description: Meditation on the Arhat in the assembly hall.

stages.name: rūpātīta
stages.description: Meditation on the formless Siddha until meditator and meditated are not two.

name: The fourteen stages of quality (guṇasthāna)

stages.name: mithyādṛṣṭi
stages.description: The soul under the rise of view-deluding karma; the approach to right view (the three processes, apunarbandhaka state) happens at its end.
stages.band_note: Starting condition, unbanded; the approach at its end (yathāpravṛtta-, apūrva-, anivṛtti-karaṇa) is B0 on other maps.

stages.name: sāsādana (sāsvādana)
stages.description: A momentary stage passed only while falling from subsidential right view toward wrong view, with a lingering taste of right view.
stages.band_note: A stage of descent only; unbanded.

stages.name: samyag-mithyādṛṣṭi (miśra)
stages.description: A mixed state of right and wrong view, like curd mixed with sugar.
stages.band_note: B0: wavering at the threshold of right view.

stages.name: avirata-samyagdṛṣṭi
stages.description: Right view (samyaktva) attained — conviction in the realities as they are, with the 'knot' broken — but without vows.
stages.band_note: B5 by the tradition's own claim that right view is the root and first real seeing of the path (the knot broken; in the Digambara adhyātma account, experience of the self); TS 1.2 defines it as conviction (śraddhāna), which on other maps would sit at B0 — contested.

stages.name: deśavirata (saṃyatāsaṃyata)
stages.description: The layman's partial vows (aṇuvrata).
stages.band_note: B1 by kind (vows), after B5 — Jainism puts right view before conduct.

stages.name: pramatta-saṃyata
stages.description: Full vows of the mendicant, with carelessness (pramāda) still arising.

stages.name: apramatta-saṃyata
stages.description: Restraint without carelessness; virtuous meditation (dharma-dhyāna) prevails.

stages.name: apūrvakaraṇa
stages.description: Beginning of the ascent on one of the two ladders (subsidence or destruction); pure meditation (śukla-dhyāna) begins.
stages.band_note: B4: first pure meditation 'with multiplicity and reasoning' still works with scriptural thought (TS 9.41-43).

stages.name: anivṛtti-bādara-sāmparāya
stages.gloss: the non-returning process with gross passion
stages.description: Gross passions are subsided or destroyed.

stages.name: sūkṣma-sāmparāya
stages.description: Only subtle greed remains.

stages.name: upaśānta-moha
stages.description: Delusion wholly subsided but not destroyed; the soul falls back from here.
stages.band_note: B6, but a dead end: from subsidence the soul necessarily falls back.

stages.name: kṣīṇa-moha
stages.description: All deluding karma destroyed; the second pure meditation (unity, without shifting); then the other destructive karmas are destroyed.

stages.name: sayoga-kevalin
stages.description: Omniscience (kevala-jñāna); the Jina lives and teaches while body, speech and mind still act.
stages.band_note: B7: kevala-jñāna is the tradition's liberation-knowledge; the teaching activity of the embodied Jina is a B8 facet.

stages.name: ayoga-kevalin
stages.description: All activity stopped for the time of uttering five short syllables; the last pure meditation; then liberation (the siddha, beyond the guṇasthānas).

equivalents.note: Umāsvāti's ten grades of karma-shedding (TS 9.45) run parallel to guṇasthānas 4-13.
Haribhadra's first four views fall within guṇasthāna 1; sthirā onward correspond to right view (4) and above; parā to kevala.
External self ~ guṇasthānas 1-3; internal self ~ 4-12; supreme self ~ 13-14 (Pūjyapāda's Samādhitantra).
The four pure meditations are distributed over guṇasthānas 8-14.

Right view (4) and stream-entry are both the first irreversible seeing that bounds the remaining rebirths; the Jain soul-doctrine and the Buddhist not-self teaching are not reconciled by this correspondence.

notes: Stage names follow the Gommaṭasāra Jīvakāṇḍa 9-10 (and the Ṣaṭkhaṇḍāgama); the Śvetāmbara lists agree in substance. The guṇasthānas are classes of soul-state by the operation of mohanīya karma and activity, not only a practice ladder: a soul may fall from 11 (and from 4 via 2). Beyond 14 the liberated soul (siddha) is outside the guṇasthānas.

name: The path of the Jewel Ornament of Liberation
notes: Chapter numbers per the usual 21-chapter division (verify). Refuge (ch.8) follows the contemplations in the text though banded as entry. Stages 9–11 are the five paths (U51's pth:five-paths) as the Jewel Ornament presents them.

name: The nine successive abidings (anupubbavihāra): four jhānas, four formless attainments, cessation

stages.name: upacāra-samādhi (commentarial)
stages.description: Unification reached just before absorption, when the hindrances are suppressed and the counterpart sign arises; not part of the canonical nine.

stages.name: paṭhama jhāna
stages.description: Secluded from sense pleasures and unwholesome states, with applied and sustained thought, rapture and bliss born of seclusion; sensual perception ceases in it.

stages.name: dutiya jhāna
stages.description: With applied and sustained thought stilled: inner confidence, unification, rapture and bliss born of concentration.

stages.name: tatiya jhāna
stages.description: With the fading of rapture, equanimous, mindful and clearly aware, he feels bliss.

stages.name: catuttha jhāna
stages.description: Pleasure and pain abandoned: neither-painful-nor-pleasant, purity of mindfulness through equanimity; in-and-out breathing ceases in it.

stages.name: ākāsānañcāyatana
stages.description: Perception of form ceases; reached by removing the kasiṇa and attending to the space left.

stages.name: viññāṇañcāyatana
stages.description: The perception of infinite space ceases.

stages.name: ākiñcaññāyatana
stages.description: The perception of infinite consciousness ceases; the attainment the bodhisatta learned from Āḷāra Kālāma.

stages.name: nevasaññānāsaññāyatana
stages.description: The perception of nothingness ceases; the attainment learned from Uddaka Rāmaputta, which the bodhisatta left because it did not lead to awakening.

stages.name: saññāvedayitanirodha (nirodha-samāpatti)
stages.description: Perception and feeling cease; the non-occurrence of consciousness and its concomitants by progressive cessation, attained only by non-returners and arahants who have the eight attainments.
stages.band_note: B6 because the commentarial tradition restricts it to noble persons who have already seen (non-returners and arahants); it is an abiding, not itself the final liberation.

equivalents.note: Graded absorptions dropping coarser factors; not claimed identical.
The Laṅkāvatāra's four dhyānas grade meditation by its object rather than by factors.

notes: The canonical list is AN 9.32 (Pali root checked locally); each attainment can also be a basis for insight (AN 9.36). The Buddha passed through all nine, up and down, at his final nibbāna (DN 16 6.8-6.9). The Abhidhamma's fivefold jhāna scheme splits the second jhāna (cpt:five-jhanas-abhidhamma).

name: Jinul's sudden awakening and gradual cultivation (tono chŏmsu)

stages.name: seeking buddha in one's own mind
stages.description: The three realms burn like a house on fire; to escape transmigration nothing is better than seeking buddha, and buddha is the mind — not outside, not apart from this body.

stages.name: tono 頓悟 (haeo 解悟)
stages.description: When a good friend points the way and in one thought one turns back the light and sees one's original nature — empty, calm, numinous knowing — it lacks nothing.
stages.band_note: B5; Jinul (after Zongmi) calls this an understanding-awakening, distinct from the realization-awakening at the end.

stages.name: chŏmsu 漸修
stages.description: Habit-energies cannot be removed at once, so relying on awakening one cultivates gradually, like an infant growing up: noticing thoughts as they arise ('do not fear thoughts arising, only fear being slow to notice'); the dual cultivation of samādhi and prajñā as substance and function of the self-nature; for the penetrated, effortless 'just thus'.

stages.name: chŭng 證 (chŭngo 證悟)
stages.description: 'All sages first awaken, then cultivate, and through cultivation realize'; phenomena are exhausted step by step as the frozen pond melts; powers appear only through gradual cultivation and are not to be used.

equivalents.note: Jinul adopts Zongmi's 'sudden awakening followed by gradual cultivation' and cites his frozen-pond simile.
Seeing the ox then taming it.
Immediate recognition for some, graded means for others.

tradition_objection: Jinul says the gates are in essence only two, sudden awakening and gradual cultivation; even 'sudden awakening, sudden cultivation' of the highest faculties rests on cultivation in past lives; principle is awakened to all at once and only phenomena are removed step by step — so the awakening itself is not a rung of a gradual ladder.
notes: Rests entirely on the Susim kyŏl (T48n2020, verified in CBETA by U42). Jinul's shortcut approach of investigating the hwadu (kyŏngjŏl mun, from the Kanhwa kyŏrŭi ron) is not included: that text is not available locally.

name: Jōdo-shū: settled mind, practice undertaken, manner of practice

stages.name: anjin (settled mind)
stages.description: Sincere, deep and dedicating mind; the conviction of birth.

stages.name: kigyō (practice undertaken)
stages.description: Chiefly calling the name, the rightly determined act.

stages.name: sagyō (manner of practice)
stages.description: Reverent, exclusive, uninterrupted, lifelong.

stages.name: right mindfulness and welcome at death (rinjū shōnen, raigō)
stages.description: Amida and the holy ones come to welcome.

stages.name: birth in the Pure Land
stages.description: Non-retrogression; seeing the Buddha.

notes: The triad comes from Shandao's question 'how to settle the mind, undertake practice and carry it out' (T1980 438c01-02, read locally); the later stages are the general Pure Land sequence.

name: The six-branch yoga (ṣaḍaṅga-yoga) of the Kālacakra

stages.name: pratyāhāra (sor sdud)
stages.description: The senses withdrawn; practised in darkness and against the open sky, ten signs appear in order — smoke, mirage, fireflies, lamp, blaze, moon, sun, darkness, lightning (kalā), drop — the 'empty forms'.

stages.name: dhyāna (bsam gtan)
stages.description: Stabilizing on the empty forms that have appeared, without imagining them ('meditation on an imagined image is not meditation for yogins').

stages.name: prāṇāyāma (srog rtsol)
stages.description: The winds of the left and right channels are brought into the central channel.
stages.band_note: Restricted practice: summary only.

stages.name: dhāraṇā ('dzin pa)
stages.description: The winds, having entered, are held in the central channel at the centres.
stages.band_note: Restricted practice: summary only.

stages.name: anusmṛti (rjes dran)
stages.description: The blazing of inner heat and the arising of bliss joined with the empty form (the 'form of the deity').
stages.band_note: B4 (still with the support of empty form); some presentations place it at the end of the path of preparation.

stages.name: samādhi (ting nge 'dzin)
stages.description: Immutable bliss inseparable from empty form; the 21,600 moments of immutable bliss consume the 21,600 karmic winds.
stages.band_note: Spans B5-B7: its first moments are counted as the path of seeing, its completion as buddhahood (low confidence on the exact correlation with the grounds).

stages.name: fruit: the Ādibuddha's gnosis
stages.description: Immutable great bliss complete; the body of empty form; the gnosis of the Ādibuddha, 'without beginning or end', not a creator.

equivalents.note: Same six branch-names in the same order (Guhyasamāja 18.138); Kālacakra gives them its own content.
Six limbs with five shared names (tarka in the Maitrī where the Kālacakra has anusmṛti).
The six branches are the Kālacakra's completion stage.

tradition_objection: The Kālacakra tradition (esp. Jonang) teaches the six branches only after the Kālacakra empowerment, the preliminaries and the lineage instructions; its wind practices are not to be attempted otherwise (Tāranātha).
notes: RESTRICTED: completion-stage energy practice — summary and the tradition's own warnings only; no methods, postures, durations or retention details. Tāranātha takes the branches in pairs: the first pair makes the empty forms appear, the middle pair brings the winds into the central channel, the last pair produces bliss and immutable bliss.

name: Kapila's sequence of devotion (Bhāgavata 3.25-29)

stages.name: sat-prasaṅga
stages.description: Attachment turned to the holy opens the door to liberation.

stages.name: kathā-śravaṇa
stages.description: In their company talks of the Lord's deeds arise, delightful to heart and ear.

stages.name: śraddhā, rati, bhakti
stages.description: Relishing them, faith, attraction and devotion follow in order.

stages.name: vairāgya and yoga
stages.gloss: dispassion and eight-limbed yoga with meditation on the Lord's form
stages.description: Devotion brings dispassion; the mind is held in yoga on the Lord.

stages.name: nirguṇa bhakti
stages.description: The mind flows to the Lord like the Gaṅgā to the sea.

stages.name: mad-bhāva
stages.description: Transcending the three guṇas, one attains the Lord; the mind reaches nirvāṇa and the body lives on while its karma lasts.

queries: local texts at the refs cited by pth:kapila-gita-bhakti-sequence

notes: Assembled by U06 from the Kapila Gītā's own ordering words (anukramiṣyati, 3.25.25); bands are interpretation-layer.

name: Kapila's yoga with a support (BhP 3.28)

stages.name: svadharma and restraints
stages.description: own dharma, contentment, service of knowers of self, non-harming, truth etc.

stages.name: āsana-jaya, prāṇa-jaya
stages.description: purifying the breath's path; breath burns faults

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: the senses drawn into the heart

stages.name: rūpa-dhyāna
stages.description: limb by limb, dwelling on glance and smile

stages.name: bhāva and release of the hook
stages.gloss: love, then letting go of the image
stages.description: melting love; the mind releases even its hook

stages.name: nirvāṇa of the mind
stages.gloss: the mind goes out like a flame
stages.description: free of support and object, the self seen as one without division

stages.name: siddha
stages.description: indifferent to the body, which lives on while karma lasts

notes: Within the Kapila Gītā (U06 owns the Gītā as a source); kept here because the coverage item names BhP 3.28.

name: The four means (upāya) of the Trika: āṇava, śākta, śāmbhava, anupāya

stages.name: āṇavopāya (kriyopāya)
stages.description: Immersion (samāveśa) through meditation on the breath (uccāra), bodily seals (karaṇa), visualization (dhyāna), letters (varṇa) and the positing of places (sthāna-kalpanā); its signs are bliss, leaping, trembling, sleep and whirling.
stages.ref: MVT 2.21; TĀ ch.5; Śiva Sūtra section 3
stages.band_note: B2 in kind (supported practices of breath, body, visualization and place), reaching B3-B4 in its own immersion.

stages.name: śāktopāya (jñānopāya)
stages.description: Immersion by contemplating with the mind alone a reality free of utterance; purification of thought-constructs (vikalpa-saṃskāra) by pure reasoning (sattarka), the teacher's instruction and scripture; the wheel of consciousness and the Kālīs.
stages.ref: MVT 2.22; TĀ ch.4; Śiva Sūtra section 2

stages.name: śāmbhavopāya (icchopāya)
stages.description: Immersion that arises for one who thinks of nothing, through the awakening given by the teacher; the universe appears in consciousness like a reflection in a mirror.
stages.ref: MVT 2.23; TĀ ch.3; Śiva Sūtra section 1

stages.name: anupāya (later also ānandopāya)
stages.description: For one of the highest grace a single hearing of the teacher's word suffices; nothing is to be done, since what is attained is one's own ever-present nature; once Śivahood is known with conviction, nothing further is to be done by any instrument.
stages.band_note: B7 by what it names (no further means; Śivahood known); the tradition does not treat it as a stage one climbs to.

equivalents.note: Both hold that recognition of one's own nature can be immediate for some while others proceed by graded means; not claimed to be the same recognition.
Dzogchen and the Trika both speak of a means-less recognition; each tradition's account of what is recognized differs and neither endorses the equation.

tradition_objection: The four are means (upāya) matched to the intensity of the descent of grace (TĀ 13), not rungs everyone must climb: the one of highest grace needs no means, and one may enter directly at śāmbhava. Abhinavagupta does teach that the lower means culminate in the higher and that difference of means does not make liberation different (TĀ 1.165-166); the Tantrāloka expounds them from the highest downward (chs. 2-5).
notes: Correction to the brief: 'anupāya' is Abhinavagupta's term (TĀ 2); the name ānandopāya for it is later. Kṣemarāja reads the three sections of the Śiva Sūtra as śāmbhava, śākta and āṇava means. The stages are listed here in ascending order for the correspondence table; the tradition's own order of exposition is descending.

name: The Kaṭha's inward withdrawal (KU 1.3.13)

stages.name: jñāna ātman → mahān ātmā

stages.name: mahān → śānta ātman
stages.description: Restrains that in the peaceful self.

stages.name: ādhāra and brahma-granthi
stages.description: Mind fixed four fingers above and at the brahma-knot; further signs and powers (KJN 14.20–37).

stages.name: hṛdaya
stages.description: Mind in the heart: samādhi with seizure and possession (KJN 14.38–43).

stages.name: kaṇṭha
stages.description: Mind at the throat-well: the scripture's truth arises in the mouth; deathlessness (KJN 14.44–49).

stages.name: lalāṭa and brahmarandhra
stages.description: Mind at the forehead and in the brahmarandhra: creator and destroyer; 'by mere knowing, through practice, one goes to liberation' (KJN 14.69–81).

stages.name: unmanī
stages.description: The mind void of void; the jīva dissolved, not roused by sound (KJN 14.82–88).

stages.name: dvādaśānta and amṛta
stages.description: The jewel-garland at the dvādaśānta; the nectar of Kaula nature; the supreme in which all dissolves; unstained by merit and sin (KJN 14.89–106).

notes: The chapter proceeds 'ataḥ ūrdhvam' (further upward) from centre to centre; ordering is the text's, stage names and bands are U21's.

stages.name: yōdō mui shin 嬰童無畏心

stages.description: Religion aimed at birth in heaven (the non-Buddhist and heavenly vehicles).

stages.name: yuiun muga shin 唯蘊無我心
stages.gloss: the mind that knows only aggregates, no self

stages.band_note: Doxographical rank of a vehicle; unbanded (cf. pth:nyingma-nine-vehicles).

stages.name: taen daijō shin 他縁大乘心
stages.gloss: the Mahāyāna mind concerned with others
stages.description: Hossō (Yogācāra).
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: kakushin fushō shin 覺心不生心
stages.gloss: the mind awakened to the unborn
stages.description: Sanron (Madhyamaka).
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: ichidō mui shin 一道無爲心
stages.gloss: the mind of the one way without action
stages.description: Tendai.
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: gokumu jishō shin 極無自性心
stages.gloss: the mind of the ultimate absence of own-nature
stages.description: Kegon.
stages.band_note: Doxographical; unbanded.

stages.name: himitsu shōgon shin 秘密莊嚴心
stages.description: Shingon: the mind as the maṇḍala; becoming a buddha in this very body.
stages.band_note: B7 as the text's goal (sokushin jōbutsu).

equivalents.note: Both rank the Buddhist vehicles in an ascending doxography culminating in the author's own tantric vehicle.

tradition_objection: Kūkai reads the ten both 'vertically' (as ascending stages, the first nine exoteric and the tenth esoteric) and 'horizontally' (all nine as aspects contained within the tenth, the maṇḍala); the ladder is a classification of teachings by depth (P5), not a practitioner's required sequence.
notes: From memory: the ten names are well known, but the text is not available locally (Taishō vol. 77). Banded only where the abode describes a practitioner's ethical or religious condition (2, 3) or the goal (10); the abodes that rank Buddhist schools are left unbanded, following U45's pth:nyingma-nine-vehicles.

name: Kumārila's way to release (Bhāṭṭa)

stages.name: kāmya-niṣiddha-varjana
stages.gloss: abstaining from desire-prompted and prohibited acts
stages.description: No new fruits requiring bodies are produced.

stages.name: nitya-naimittika-anuṣṭhāna
stages.description: To avoid the demerit of omission; Tantravārttika: also to destroy past sin.

stages.name: ātmajñāna
stages.description: Knowing the self (made firm by Vedānta); the self-knower no longer desires the fruits, so they do not accrue.

stages.name: bhoga (pūrvakriyākṣaya)
stages.description: Past karma is used up by experiencing its fruits.

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: With no accumulation left no body arises; for Pārthasārathi, the absolute dissolution of the threefold bond, without bliss.

notes: The order is logical rather than strictly temporal (stages 1-4 run concurrently). Band B5 for self-knowledge is at most 'analogous': Kumārila does not treat it as a liberating insight.

stages.name: brahmagranthi-vibhedinī

name: The three visions of the Lamdre

stages.name: impure vision
stages.description: Appearances of beings under the afflictions; contemplated as the faults of saṃsāra, leisure and endowment, death and karma to turn the mind.

stages.name: experiential vision
stages.description: Appearances to the yogin in concentration; love, compassion, bodhicitta and the meditative experiences of the path.

stages.name: pure vision
stages.description: The inexhaustible ornamental wheel of the Sugatas' body, speech and mind.

notes: Bands: the three visions are also taught as simultaneous perspectives, not only successive stages; banding is approximate.

name: The path through the grounds in the Vajra Verses

stages.name: path of accumulation
stages.description: Freed from the ordinary body, speech and mind by the four results; the elements gather.

stages.name: path of joining (heat, peak, patience, supreme dharma)
stages.description: The path of the inner buddhas reaching the peak of existence; patience of the unborn.

stages.name: first ground
stages.description: Marked by inner and outer signs (one finger-width of wind ceasing; drop stabilised).

stages.name: second to sixth grounds
stages.gloss: sa gnyis pa – sa drug pa
stages.description: Emanation-body qualities increase; six finger-widths of wind cease.

stages.name: seventh to tenth grounds
stages.gloss: sa bdun pa – sa bcu pa
stages.description: Enjoyment-body qualities; mastery of speech and teaching; ten finger-widths of wind cease.

stages.name: eleventh and twelfth grounds
stages.description: Dharmakāya qualities; twelve finger-widths of wind cease.

stages.name: twelve-and-a-half ground
stages.description: The life-wind enters the avadhūtī; the eight qualities of mastery arise.

stages.name: thirteenth ground, Vajradhara
stages.gloss: sa bcu gsum pa rdo rje 'dzin pa
stages.description: Omniscience; awakening with a retinue.

notes: Reconstructed from the terse Tibetan of Tōh 2284 (local); the signs belong to restricted completion-stage practice and are summarised only. Ground groupings follow markers in the root text ('sa drug', 'sa bcu', 'sa bcu gnyis', 'sa phyed dang bcu gsum', 'bcu gsum'); low confidence.

name: The stages of the path for persons of the three scopes (lam rim; skyes bu gsum)

stages.name: reliance on the spiritual teacher
stages.description: Proper reliance on a qualified teacher in thought and deed.

stages.name: leisure and endowment
stages.description: Its great value and rarity: free of the eight unfree states, with the ten endowments.

stages.name: small scope: death and the lower realms
stages.description: Mindfulness of death (certain, its time uncertain, only dharma helps) and the sufferings of the lower realms.

stages.name: small scope: refuge and karma
stages.gloss: refuge and the ethics of action
stages.description: Going for refuge (from fear of the lower realms and faith); the four characteristics of karma; abandoning the ten non-virtues.
stages.band_note: Refuge itself is B0; the ethics of karma is B1.

stages.name: middle scope: the faults of saṃsāra and renunciation
stages.description: The eight and six sufferings, the origin in the afflictions; renunciation arises when one wishes for liberation day and night like a prisoner.
stages.band_note: B0: each scope opens with a turning of the mind; the Lamrim is therefore non-monotonic by design.

stages.name: middle scope: the three trainings
stages.description: Ethics, concentration and wisdom, with ethics as their foundation.

stages.name: great scope: the mind of awakening
stages.description: The seven-point cause-and-effect instruction and the exchange of self and other; adopting the aspiring and engaging mind of awakening by ritual.

stages.name: great scope: the deeds
stages.gloss: six perfections and four ways of gathering
stages.description: The bodhisattva vow; the six perfections ripen one's own continuum, the four ways of gathering ripen others.

stages.name: calm abiding
stages.description: The nine mental states, six powers and four attentions, to calm abiding proper with pliancy.

stages.name: insight
stages.description: Identifying the object of negation and establishing the selflessness of persons and phenomena by Prāsaṅgika reasoning; insight proper when analysis itself induces pliancy and calm and insight are unified.
stages.band_note: B4 by this unit's rule: the union of calm and insight on emptiness is still conceptual (it marks the path of preparation in Tsongkhapa's account); the direct seeing is the path of seeing (B5, pth:five-paths).

stages.name: entering the Vajrayāna
stages.description: Having trained in the paths common to sūtra and tantra, one should enter the Vajrayāna: empowerment from a qualified master, guarding vows and pledges, the two stages.
stages.band_note: Unbanded: the Lamrim hands over to the Ngagrim; see pth:vajrayana-two-stages.

equivalents.note: Tsongkhapa's condensation: renunciation (middle scope), the mind of awakening (great scope), the correct view (insight).
Gampopa's Jewel Ornament (Kagyu) follows the same Kadam stages.
The Sakya 'parting from the four attachments' condenses the same scopes.
The Nyingma outer preliminaries cover the same ground as the small and middle scopes.
Expands stage 7.

notes: Atiśa's Bodhipathapradīpa defines the three persons (v2-5); Tsongkhapa's Lamrim Chenmo gives the full stages. The first two stages are 'the foundation'; each scope begins with its own turning of mind, which is why the bands return to B0 three times.

stages.description: Śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha yogis contemplating the no-self of persons, impermanence, suffering and impurity up to cessation

stages.name: tāthāgata-dhyāna

stages.name: hearing the name and rejoicing, even one thought
stages.description: Gains the great benefit.

stages.name: aspiration, recollection, merit (the three grades)
stages.description: Arousing bodhicitta, recollecting Amitāyus, doing good according to capacity.

stages.name: welcome at death
stages.description: Amitābha appears with the assembly (19th vow).

stages.name: birth by transformation; the rightly established group
stages.description: Necessary attainment of nirvāṇa (11th vow); non-retrogression.

stages.name: one life from buddhahood
stages.description: Bodhisattvas there reach the stage of one-life replacement (22nd vow).

stages.name: buddhahood / nirvāṇa
stages.description: Extinction (miedu) reached necessarily.

stages.name: returning to save beings
stages.description: Those who by their own vow choose to teach in other lands, practising Samantabhadra's virtue.

stages.name: Relying on mind-only
stages.description: Understanding that external objects do not exist.

stages.name: Relying on the Madhyamaka
stages.description: Understanding that even mind is utterly without self.

stages.name: Riding the two chariots
stages.description: Holding the reins of reasoning over both systems, one is a true Mahāyānist.

name: The ten grounds of the Madhyamakāvatāra

stages.name: Before the grounds: compassion, non-dual understanding and the awakening mind
stages.description: The ordinary bodhisattva cultivates compassion, the awakening mind and non-dual understanding (MA 1.1–2); hearing emptiness with joy marks a fit vessel (MA 6.4–5).

stages.name: Pramuditā
stages.description: The first ground, on which the perfection of giving (dāna) predominates. Emptiness is seen directly for the first time; the bodhisattva rejoices, having become a child of the Victors.

stages.name: Vimalā
stages.description: The second ground, on which the perfection of discipline (śīla) predominates.

stages.name: Prabhākarī
stages.description: The third ground, on which the perfection of patience (kṣānti) predominates.

stages.name: Arciṣmatī
stages.description: The fourth ground, on which the perfection of vigour (vīrya) predominates.

stages.name: Sudurjayā
stages.description: The fifth ground, on which the perfection of meditation (dhyāna) predominates.

stages.name: Abhimukhī
stages.description: The sixth ground, on which the perfection of wisdom (prajñā) predominates. Here the long exposition of emptiness (MA 6) is given; the bodhisattva can enter cessation.

stages.name: Dūraṃgamā
stages.description: The seventh ground, on which the perfection of method (upāya) predominates.

stages.name: Acalā
stages.description: The eighth ground, on which the perfection of aspiration (praṇidhāna) predominates. The bodhisattva is irreversible and no longer moved by conceptual effort.

stages.name: Sādhumatī
stages.description: The ninth ground, on which the perfection of power (bala) predominates.

stages.name: Dharmameghā
stages.description: The tenth ground, on which the perfection of knowledge (jñāna) predominates.

stages.name: The Buddha ground
stages.description: The qualities of the grounds culminate in buddhahood, with the bodies and activity of a Buddha, who remains for beings without abiding in nirvāṇa.

notes: Ground names confirmed for grounds 1, 4 and 5 in the local e-text of the bhāṣya; the others and their pairing with the ten perfections follow the Daśabhūmika tradition (pth:ten-bhumis).

stages.description: Middling level of one taste.

stages.name: ro gcig (ekarasa) — greater
stages.description: Greater level of one taste.

stages.name: sgom med (abhāvanā) — lesser
stages.description: Nothing to meditate and no meditator; the natural state without contrivance; at its greatest, the dharmakāya fully manifest.

stages.name: sgom med (abhāvanā) — middling
stages.description: Middling level of non-meditation.

stages.name: sgom med (abhāvanā) — greater
stages.description: Greater level of non-meditation.
stages.band_note: Greater non-meditation = buddhahood (the fruition dharmakāya).

equivalents.note: Expands stage 7 of U46's Moonbeams map.
Tilopa's torrent–river–ocean describes the same deepening in three images.
Kagyu masters correlate the four yogas with the five paths and ten grounds differently; Moonbeams records the views.
Drikung's fivefold Mahāmudrā arranges the same practice by five points rather than stages.

tradition_objection: Mahāmudrā teachers stress that the nature of mind is not produced by the yogas: 'no path to travel', 'if you attain non-attainment you attain Mahāmudrā' (Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā); the four yogas describe the ripening of recognition and are said to arise in different orders for gradual and simultaneous persons.
notes: The twelve levels are given as in Dakpo Tashi Namgyal's Moonbeams; descriptions of the middling and greater levels are kept generic because they were not recalled with confidence. The correlations with the five paths differ among Kagyu masters (tea:moonbeams-of-mahamudra:pt.2/7).

name: Maharshi Mehi's graded practice

stages.name: mānas jap
stages.description: Mental repetition of the name.

stages.name: mānas dhyān
stages.description: Contemplating the guru's or deity's form.

stages.name: dṛṣṭi yoga
stages.description: Fixing the gaze at a point within, opening the inner light.

stages.name: nādānusandhān
stages.description: Following the inner sounds to the soundless.

stages.name: niḥśabda
stages.description: Beyond sound: realization of the Supreme.

name: Mahāsi Sayadaw's progress of insight through noting

stages.name: sīla-visuddhi
stages.description: The meditator first purifies conduct (precepts) before the retreat.

stages.name: citta-visuddhi by khaṇika-samādhi
stages.gloss: purification of mind by momentary concentration
stages.description: Continuous, precise noting of whatever arises (beginning with the rising and falling of the abdomen) builds momentary concentration strong enough for insight, in place of jhāna.
stages.ref: Practical Insight Meditation; Progress of Insight
stages.band_note: B3; the tradition holds that momentary concentration does the work of access concentration for the pure-insight practitioner.

stages.name: knowledges 1-3
stages.description: The noted object and the noting mind are distinguished, their conditionality seen, and they are comprehended as impermanent, painful, not-self; unpleasant sensations are often prominent.

stages.name: knowledge 4
stages.description: Bright lights, rapture, tranquillity, happiness, strong faith and quick noting may appear; attachment to them is the corruption of insight to be noted and passed.

stages.name: knowledges 5-10
stages.gloss: dissolution, fearfulness, misery, disgust, desire for deliverance, re-observation
stages.description: Only vanishing is seen; formations appear fearful, full of danger and wearisome; a desire for deliverance arises; re-observation.

stages.name: knowledge 11
stages.description: Noting proceeds by itself, smoothly and without effort, neither delighting nor fearing, and can last long.

stages.name: knowledges 12-13
stages.description: Insight leading to emergence culminates in conformity and then in change-of-lineage.
stages.band_note: Conformity is B4 and change-of-lineage B5 on pth:sixteen-insight-knowledges; grouped here as the threshold.

stages.name: knowledges 14-15
stages.description: The noted objects and the noting mind cease: the cessation of formations (nibbāna) is experienced.

stages.name: knowledge 16 and after
stages.gloss: reviewing; fruition attainment; the higher paths
stages.description: Reviewing knowledge follows; the meditator may practise entering fruition and continue insight for the higher paths.

equivalents.note: Same sixteen knowledges presented through the practice of noting.

notes: Post-1800 teacher (recent). Kept separate from pth:sixteen-insight-knowledges because Mahāsi's account describes the stages as they appear in noting practice (momentary concentration instead of jhāna, typical experiences at each stage). Grouping of knowledges follows the chapter's own grouping as recalled; moderate confidence on the grouping.

name: Realization, meditation, conduct (the siddhas' sequence)

stages.name: rtogs pa skyed
stages.description: First the intelligent generate realization (from the true guru).

stages.name: gnas lugs ma yengs sgom
stages.gloss: undistracted meditation on the natural state
stages.description: Meditating without distraction; making all appearances undivided.

stages.name: spyod pa
stages.description: When experience has arisen, practising conduct with care — for Mekopa the cremation ground and the 'mad' observance.

name: The four conducts of the bodhisattva (Mahāvastu)

stages.name: prakṛticaryā
stages.description: Planting roots of merit before a Buddha (under Aparājitadhvaja).

stages.name: praṇidhānacaryā
stages.description: The first vow to become a Buddha (under a former Śākyamuni).

stages.name: anulomacaryā
stages.description: Conduct in accordance with the vow (under Samitāvin).

stages.name: anivartanacaryā
stages.description: After Dīpaṅkara's prediction.

name: The ten grounds of the bodhisattva (Mahāvastu)

stages.name: durārohā
stages.description: The first ground; the text details the conduct and the qualities that lead to it.

stages.name: durjayā
stages.description: From the seventh ground the bodhisattva does not turn back (low confidence).

stages.name: abhiṣeka
stages.description: The tenth ground (abhiṣekavatī) ends at Mvu i.193.
