name: The four vidyādhara levels of Mahāyoga

stages.name: rnam smin rig 'dzin
stages.description: The mind matured as the deity while the body is not yet transformed.

stages.name: tshe dbang rig 'dzin
stages.description: The body transformed into a vajra body free of birth and death.

stages.name: phyag chen rig 'dzin
stages.description: Arising in the deity's form of union on the path of meditation.

stages.name: lhun grub rig 'dzin
stages.description: The final fruit, equal to buddhahood.

notes: Correspondence to the five paths and the bands is the unit's low-confidence reconstruction.

name: The six-limbed yoga of the Maitrī Upaniṣad (ṣaḍaṅga-yoga)

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: First limb of the method (prayoga-kalpa) for union with the self.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: The mind withdrawn from outer things and the objects placed within (6.19).

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Named before dhāraṇā in this list.
stages.band_note: The Maitrī's order puts dhyāna before dhāraṇā; both banded B3.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: The 'further concentration' of 6.20: pressing the tongue-tip to the palate, restraining speech, mind and breath.

stages.name: tarka
stages.description: A limb peculiar to this list; in 6.20 'by tarka one sees brahman'.
stages.band_note: B4 as discernment still working with an object; the seeing it leads to is stage 7.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Last limb; the mind placed in what is not mind, the inconceivable, without support (6.19).

stages.name: seeing the golden-hued maker
stages.description: By this yoga the seer sees the golden-coloured maker, the lord, the person, the source of brahman (brahmayoni); through the dissolution of mind one sees the self, subtler than the subtle, shining (6.20).

stages.name: making all one in the imperishable
stages.description: The knower, leaving merit and evil, makes all one in the highest imperishable; faults do not approach him, as deer and birds avoid a burning mountain; selflessness is 'the mark of liberation' (6.20).

equivalents.note: Same count of six and three shared limb-names (pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, samādhi) in a different order, with anusmṛti for tarka; no historical claim is made here.
As above: six limbs with five shared names; Kālacakra has anusmṛti where the Maitrī has tarka.
Nātha six-limbed yoga (āsana instead of tarka).
Six-limbed yoga of the Yoga Upaniṣads.
The Amṛtanāda Upaniṣad's six limbs (pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, tarka, samādhi) keep tarka as in the Maitrī.

notes: Stage names and order verified against the local e-text (Cowell recension, ebharati): prāṇāyāmaḥ pratyāhāro dhyānaṃ dhāraṇā tarkaḥ samādhiḥ ṣaḍaṅga ity ucyate yogaḥ (6.18). Stages 7-8 are the fruit stated in the same section; they are added so that the map reaches its own goal.

name: From dharma to liberation (Rāmcaritmānas 3.16)

stages.name: dharma
stages.description: Keeping one's dharma.

stages.name: virati
stages.description: From dharma comes dispassion.

stages.name: yoga
stages.description: Yoga practised in dispassion.

stages.name: jñāna
stages.description: From yoga comes knowledge.

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: Knowledge gives liberation, as the Vedas say — but devotion, which melts the Lord at once, is set above this sequence.

name: The lamp of knowledge (Rāmcaritmānas 7.117–118)

stages.name: sāttvika śraddhā (the cow)
stages.description: Faith comes to dwell in the heart by Hari's grace.

stages.name: japa, tapa, vrata, yama-niyama (the grass)
stages.description: Faith is nourished by repetition, austerity, vows, restraints and Vedic good conduct.

stages.name: bhāva (the calf) and the milk of dharma
stages.description: Loving disposition draws forth the milk of highest dharma, milked by a pure mind into the vessel of trust.

stages.name: boiling, cooling and setting
stages.description: Boiled on desirelessness, cooled by contentment and forgiveness, set with fortitude and equanimity.

stages.name: churning by vicāra; the butter of vairāgya
stages.description: Churned by reflection with self-control and truthful speech, it yields pure dispassion.

stages.name: the fire of yoga; the ghee of jñāna
stages.description: Melted in yoga, burning good and bad karma, it becomes knowledge, 'mine-ness' burnt away.

stages.name: the lamp: citta, samatā, turīya wick
stages.description: Knowledge poured into the mind set on equanimity with the wick of the fourth state.

stages.name: so'ham asmi (the flame)
stages.description: The Self's experience shines and the delusion of difference, root of existence, is destroyed — unless māyā's powers and the senses blow the lamp out.

notes: The Mānas presents this path of knowledge in order to set above it devotion, the self-luminous gem that needs none of these stages and cannot be blown out (7.119–120).

name: Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa: eight limbs, tāraka and amanaska

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Conquering cold, heat, food and sleep; calm; sense-restraint.

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Devotion to guru, contentment, solitude, dispassion.

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: A comfortable seat.

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: Counts not reproduced.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Withdrawal of mind from objects.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Fixing the mind on consciousness.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: One-pointedness on the consciousness in all bodies.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Forgetting of meditation.

stages.name: tāraka
stages.description: Seeing the three targets and lights; śāmbhavī.

stages.name: amanaska
stages.description: Mind like an udder after milking; 'you are I'.

stages.name: paramahaṃsa avadhūta
stages.description: Mind dissolved in the supreme state of Viṣṇu; acts like a child or madman; sight purifies the world.

name: The Vedic course of dharma (Mīmāṃsā account)

stages.name: vedādhyayana
stages.gloss: study of one's Vedic recension from a teacher
stages.description: The student learns the Veda by the injunction of study.

stages.name: dharma-jijñāsā
stages.description: Before returning home the student inquires into the meaning of the Vedic sentences.

stages.name: agnyādhāna
stages.description: Becoming eligible (with one's wife) for the śrauta rites.

stages.name: nitya-naimittika karma
stages.description: Rites such as the Agnihotra and the new- and full-moon offerings, performed for life.

stages.name: svarga
stages.description: The fruit of the rites, understood as happiness; the self, not the burnt body, attains it.

stages.name: thun mong gi sngon 'gro
stages.description: the four thoughts

stages.name: thun mong ma yin pa'i sngon 'gro
stages.description: refuge and bodhicitta, Vajrasattva, maṇḍala, guru yoga

stages.name: rten bcas zhi gnas
stages.description: object, breath or deity

stages.name: lhag mthong
stages.description: looking at the mind in stillness and movement

stages.name: ngo sprod

stages.description: sustaining and perfecting the recognition (see pth:mahamudra-four-yogas)

stages.name: 'bras bu
stages.description: the dharmakāya in non-meditation

name: The limbs of yoga in the Mṛgendra (seven auxiliaries and yoga as the eighth)

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: exertion of breath by propelling, drawing in and holding; removes faults of ritual

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: turning the mind back from all objects once it tastes a little ease

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: the withdrawn mind fixed on a place chosen at will

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: thought directed again and again on that object

stages.name: vīkṣaṇa (ūha)
stages.description: scrutiny of the object: what is to be rejected and accepted, what sustains and opposes it

stages.name: japa
stages.description: uttering (its mantra), bringing the object of meditation face to face

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: when meditation becomes one continuous flow

stages.name: yoga (aṅgin)
stages.description: the eighth, the possessor of the limbs; powers shine forth like the sun's rays

name: Muktikā: the path to liberation

stages.name: sādhana-catuṣṭaya
stages.description: Discrimination, dispassion, six virtues, longing for liberation.

stages.name: sadguru
stages.description: Approach with gifts; be tested.

stages.name: graded study
stages.description: Study as much as needed for knowledge to arise.

stages.name: śravaṇa
stages.description: Hearing the Upaniṣads from the teacher.

stages.name: manana
stages.description: Reflecting on what is heard.

stages.name: nididhyāsana
stages.description: Contemplation, with destruction of vāsanā and dissolution of mind.

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: Mind dissolved 'with form'; prārabdha continues.

stages.name: videhamukti
stages.description: At the body's fall, like pot-space or wind becoming still.

name: Who crosses māyā: the Nārada Bhakti Sūtra's sequence (NBS 46–50)

stages.name: saṅga-tyāga, mahānubhāva-sevā, nirmamatā
stages.gloss: giving up attachments, serving the great, freedom from 'mine'
stages.description: One who gives up attachments, serves the great souls and becomes free of 'mine'.

stages.name: vivikta-sthāna, loka-bandha-unmūlana, nistraiguṇya, yoga-kṣema-tyāga
stages.gloss: solitude, uprooting worldly bonds, going beyond the guṇas, giving up acquiring and keeping
stages.description: Resorting to a solitary place, uprooting the bonds of the world, going beyond the three guṇas, giving up the concern to acquire and keep.

stages.name: karma-phala-tyāga, karma-saṃnyāsa, nirdvandvatā
stages.gloss: giving up fruits, renouncing actions, then freedom from the pairs
stages.description: Giving up the fruit of actions, renouncing actions, and 'then' (tataḥ) becoming free of the pairs of opposites.

stages.name: veda-saṃnyāsa
stages.description: Renouncing even the Vedas (their ritual injunctions), laid down in the Lord.

stages.name: avicchinna-anurāga
stages.description: Obtaining unbroken, uninterrupted love.

stages.name: tarati
stages.description: He crosses (māyā), he crosses.

stages.name: lokāṃs tārayati
stages.description: He brings the worlds across.

notes: The sūtras list marks in groups; 'tataḥ' (then) in NBS 48 and the culmination in 49–50 suggest a sequence, which is how it is laid out here. Bands are interpretation-layer claims. The Nārada Sūtra also distinguishes secondary (gauṇī) from primary devotion (cpt:gauni-and-para-bhakti), not staged further.

name: The ascent of the liberated through the four forms (Nārāyaṇīya)

stages.name: freedom from merit and demerit
stages.description: Those free of fault, beyond merit and demerit, take the safe road (12.332.13).

stages.name: the sun as door
stages.description: The sun is the door; burnt by it, atom-like and invisible, they enter that god (12.332.13–14).

stages.name: Aniruddha
stages.description: Freed from the sun they abide in Aniruddha's body (12.332.15).

stages.name: Pradyumna
stages.description: Becoming mind, they enter Pradyumna (12.332.15).

stages.name: Saṃkarṣaṇa
stages.description: Freed from Pradyumna they enter the jīva Saṃkarṣaṇa — Sāṃkhyas together with Bhāgavatas (12.332.16).

stages.name: Vāsudeva
stages.description: Free of the three guṇas they enter the supreme self, the knower of the field, Vāsudeva, the dwelling of all; the one-pointed enter Vāsudeva directly (12.332.17–18; 12.336.3).

notes: A path of the liberated after death, not a sequence of practices; intermediate stages are left without bands. Janamejaya's question (12.336.3–4) calls the vyūha route the 'fourth path' and the ekāntins' direct entry the highest.

name: The stages of Nāth initiation

stages.name: approach and service
stages.description: Seeking a guru, being tested and serving (warned of the hardships).

stages.name: first initiation (aughaṛ)
stages.description: The guru cuts the top-knot, gives the mantra and the selī cord.

stages.name: probation
stages.description: A period of service and discipline under the guru.

stages.name: ear-splitting (darśanī / kānphaṭa)
stages.description: The ears are split and the earrings worn; a new name ending in -nāth and a panth.

name: The nine grades of birth (Contemplation Sūtra 14–16)

stages.name: upper grade, upper birth
stages.gloss: three minds; precepts, Mahāyāna sūtras, six recollections
stages.description: Welcomed by Amitābha and the assembly; on birth at once sees the Buddha and awakens to the acceptance of non-arising.

stages.name: upper grade, middle birth
stages.gloss: understands the meaning of the Mahāyāna
stages.description: Lotus opens overnight; non-retrogression after seven days; acceptance of non-arising after one small kalpa.

stages.name: upper grade, lower birth
stages.gloss: believes cause and effect, arouses bodhicitta
stages.description: Lotus opens after a day and night; sees the Buddha clearly after three weeks; after three small kalpas enters the ground of joy.

stages.name: middle grade, upper birth
stages.gloss: keeps the five and eight precepts
stages.description: At once attains arhatship.

stages.name: middle grade, middle birth
stages.gloss: keeps precepts for a day and night
stages.description: Becomes a stream-enterer; an arhat after half a kalpa.

stages.name: middle grade, lower birth
stages.description: Meets the two bodhisattvas after seven days, becomes a stream-enterer; an arhat after a small kalpa.

stages.name: lower grade, upper birth
stages.gloss: evil-doer who does not slander the Mahāyāna; calls the name once at death
stages.description: Lotus opens after forty-nine days; after ten small kalpas enters the first ground.

stages.name: lower grade, middle birth
stages.gloss: precept-breaker; hears of the Buddha's virtues at death
stages.description: Hell-fires become a cool wind; lotus opens after six kalpas; arouses the aspiration for awakening.

stages.name: lower grade, lower birth
stages.gloss: five offences and ten evils; ten recitations at death
stages.description: Lotus opens after twelve great kalpas; the two bodhisattvas teach the real mark; arouses the aspiration for awakening.

notes: Grades read locally in T365. Bands are assigned by the practitioner's conduct in this life (upper: Mahāyāna practice; middle: precepts; lower: evil-doers saved at death); for Shandao all nine are ordinary beings.

name: The nine stages of settling the mind (navākārā cittasthiti) leading to calm abiding

stages.name: cittasthāpana / sems 'jog pa
stages.description: The mind is placed on the object (by the power of hearing). [power; attention: hearing; forced attention]

stages.name: saṃsthāpana / rgyun du 'jog pa
stages.description: Placed for a little longer (power of reflection). [power; attention: reflection; forced attention]

stages.name: avasthāpana / glan te 'jog pa
stages.description: Distraction noticed quickly and the mind patched back (mindfulness). [power; attention: mindfulness; interrupted attention]

stages.name: upasthāpana / nye bar 'jog pa
stages.description: The mind withdrawn inward ever more; the object no longer lost (mindfulness). [power; attention: mindfulness; interrupted attention]

stages.name: damana / dul bar byed pa
stages.description: Delighting the mind in concentration by seeing its qualities (alertness). [power; attention: alertness; interrupted attention]

stages.name: śamana / zhi bar byed pa
stages.description: Quelling displeasure toward concentration (alertness). [power; attention: alertness; interrupted attention]

stages.name: vyupaśamana / rnam par zhi bar byed pa
stages.description: Pacifying even subtle attachment, sinking and agitation as they arise (effort). [power; attention: effort; interrupted attention]

stages.name: ekotīkaraṇa / rtse gcig tu byed pa
stages.description: Continuous concentration with a little effort at the start (effort). [power; attention: effort; uninterrupted attention]

stages.name: samādhāna / mnyam par 'jog pa
stages.description: Effortless, spontaneous concentration (familiarity). [power; attention: complete familiarity; spontaneous attention]
stages.band_note: B3: before pliancy arises the ninth state is only a 'likeness' of calm abiding (LRCM).

stages.name: śamatha proper (with pliancy)
stages.description: After the ninth state mental and then physical pliancy arise with their joy; when the joy settles the mind rests stably on its object at will — calm abiding proper, the preparation for the first dhyāna.

equivalents.note: The Śrāvakabhūmi's seven attentions continue from calm abiding into the dhyānas.
Kamalaśīla's stages embed the same nine settlings.
Mahāmudrā śamatha uses the nine settlings (Moonbeams).
Calm abiding proper corresponds to access to the first dhyāna in both Abhidharma systems.

notes: Sanskrit names as in the Śrāvakabhūmi (sthāpayati, saṃsthāpayati, avasthāpayati, upasthāpayati, damayati, śamayati, vyupaśamayati, ekotīkaroti, samādadhāti; nominal forms given); Tibetan as in the Lamrim literature. The six powers and four attentions are given per stage as the Lamrim Chenmo distributes them.

name: The noble eightfold path as defined in DN 22

stages.name: sammādiṭṭhi

stages.name: sammāsaṅkappa

stages.name: sammāvācā
stages.description: abstaining from false, divisive, harsh speech and idle chatter

name: The Nyāya path to liberation (apavarga)

stages.name: jñānagrahaṇābhyāsa / śravaṇa
stages.gloss: study of the science of the self
stages.description: Study, retention, listening and reflection on the science of the self (NS 4.2.47; NBh).

stages.name: ātmasaṃskāra: yama and niyama
stages.description: Restraints common to all life-stages and particular observances remove demerit and increase merit (NS 4.2.46; NBh).

stages.name: saṃvāda / manana
stages.description: Discussion with the learned and reasoned examination through the sixteen categories, to cut doubt and confirm what is ascertained (NS 4.2.47–49; NK 1.3).

stages.name: yoga and adhyātmavidhi
stages.gloss: yoga in solitude; the method of the inner self
stages.description: Yoga in forests, caves and sandbanks; austerity, breath-control, sense-withdrawal, meditation, fixation; contemplation of objects and of the body (prasaṅkhyāna) (NS 4.2.42, 4.2.46; NBh 4.2.2, 4.2.46).

stages.name: samādhiviśeṣābhyāsa
stages.description: Repeated practice of a special samādhi, from which knowledge of truth arises (NS 4.2.38).

stages.name: tattvajñāna
stages.description: Knowledge of the self and the other objects of knowledge as they are; the I-notion ceases (NS 1.1.1, 4.2.1; NBh 1.1.1).

stages.name: removal of false knowledge, faults and activity
stages.gloss: the chain undone; the detached dweller
stages.description: False knowledge removed, faults, activity and further birth fall away (NS 1.1.2); for one whose afflictions have waned, activity does not lead to rebirth (NS 4.1.64); one who dwells detached within and without is called liberated (NBh 4.2.2).

stages.name: apavarga
stages.description: With birth ended, pain ends absolutely: liberation (NS 1.1.22).

notes: The order is a reconstruction from separate sūtras (the texts do not number stages). Bands are interpretive; stage 7 is given B8 because the Bhāṣya calls the detached dweller 'liberated' while embodied, before final release (B7).

name: The nine vehicles (theg pa rim pa dgu)

stages.name: śrāvakayāna
stages.description: Renunciation, ethics and insight into selflessness of the person; nirvāṇa as arhatship.

stages.name: pratyekabuddhayāna
stages.description: Realization of dependent origination; selflessness of the person and part of phenomena.

stages.name: bodhisattvayāna
stages.description: Bodhicitta, the six perfections, the two selflessnesses; the five paths and ten grounds.

stages.name: kriyātantra
stages.description: Outer tantra: purity, ritual and the deity seen as lord and servant.

stages.name: ubhayatantra / caryātantra
stages.description: Outer tantra: the deity as friend; view of yoga, conduct of kriyā.

stages.name: yogatantra
stages.description: Outer tantra: union with the deity in meditation.

stages.name: mahāyoga
stages.description: Inner tantra: generation stage; great purity and equality.

stages.name: anuyoga
stages.description: Inner tantra: completion stage; union of expanse and wisdom.

stages.name: atiyoga
stages.description: Awareness itself: cutting through and direct crossing.

notes: The nine vehicles are a doxographical hierarchy (each vehicle a complete path for its practitioners) rather than successive stages of one person's progress; interpretive bands are therefore not assigned.

name: The Pa-Auk sequence of calm and insight

stages.name: sīla
stages.description: Monastic or lay precepts kept purely.

stages.name: ānāpānasati to the fourth jhāna (or four-elements meditation to access)
stages.description: Breath with bright nimitta to jhāna; or the twelve characteristics of the elements.

stages.name: further samatha (optional)
stages.description: Kasiṇas, formless attainments, immeasurables, recollections.

stages.name: rūpa-kammaṭṭhāna
stages.description: Seeing material groups and analysing their elements in all six doors.

stages.name: nāma-kammaṭṭhāna
stages.description: Discerning the mind-moments and mental factors of cognitive processes.

stages.name: paṭiccasamuppāda
stages.description: Discerning causes in past lives and results in future lives.

stages.name: vipassanā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Comprehension, rise and fall and the further knowledges as in the Visuddhimagga.

stages.name: magga-phala
stages.description: Realization of nibbāna.

notes: Assigning B5 to the discernment of ultimate realities (before the paths) is an interpretive choice: it is 'seeing' in the Visuddhimagga's sense of purification of view, not stream-entry.

name: The seven states of the jīva (Pañcadaśī 7)

stages.name: ajñāna
stages.description: not knowing the self (the ten men not counting themselves)

stages.name: āvaraṇa
stages.description: 'the tenth is not there, it does not shine'

stages.name: vikṣepa
stages.description: grief, wrong notions ('the tenth is lost')

stages.name: parokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: 'there is a tenth' — knowledge from the teacher's word not yet one's own

stages.name: aparokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: 'you are the tenth' — recognizing oneself as Brahman

stages.name: śoka-nivṛtti
stages.description: grief ends with recognition

stages.name: niraṅkuśa-tṛpti
stages.description: the satisfaction of one who has done all that is to be done (jīvanmukti)

notes: Illustrated by the tenth-man story. Bands are interpretive.

name: The five stages of the Pañcakrama (Ārya Guhyasamāja)

stages.name: utpattikrama
stages.description: The practitioner established in the generation stage.

stages.name: vajrajāpa (vāgviveka)
stages.description: Mantra joined with the winds.

stages.name: sarvaśuddhiviśuddhi (cittaviveka)
stages.description: The three appearances and four empties with the eighty natural conceptions.

stages.name: svādhiṣṭhāna
stages.description: The illusory body, conventional truth, by the guru's grace.

stages.name: abhisambodhi
stages.description: Clear light, the all-empty, ultimate truth.

stages.name: yuganaddha
stages.description: Union of illusory body and clear light; buddhahood as Vajradhara.

name: Learning, childlikeness, silence (BAU 3.5.1)
description: The stages of the knower who has renounced, as stated to Kahola.

stages.name: vyutthāna
stages.description: Knowing the self, brahmins rise above the desires for sons, wealth and worlds and live as mendicants.

stages.name: pāṇḍitya
stages.description: Having done with learning ...

stages.name: bālya
stages.description: ... he should live as a child.

stages.name: mauna
stages.description: Having done with childhood and learning, he becomes a silent sage.

stages.name: brāhmaṇa
stages.description: Having done with silence and non-silence, he becomes a brahmin.

notes: The meaning of bālya (childlike state; Śaṅkara relates it to the strength of knowledge) is not settled; no band.

checks.note: Located: BĀU 3.5.1 ('tasmād brāhmaṇaḥ pāṇḍityaṃ nirvidya bālyena tiṣṭhāset | bālyaṃ ca pāṇḍityaṃ ca nirvidyātha muniḥ | amaunaṃ ca maunaṃ ca nirvidyātha brāhmaṇaḥ'). name: The nine steps to the supreme abode (Paramapadasopānam)

stages.name: viveka
stages.description: Discerning self from body and the Lord as master.

stages.name: nirveda
stages.description: Grief at one's past and at worldly life.

stages.name: virakti
stages.description: Turning away from lesser ends.

stages.name: bhīti
stages.description: Fear of continued rebirth.

stages.name: prasādana (prasāda-hetu)
stages.description: Surrender, which wins the Lord's grace.

stages.name: utkramaṇa
stages.description: Leaving the body through the head channel.

stages.name: arcirādi
stages.description: Travelling by the path of light.

stages.name: divyadeśa-prāpti
stages.description: Arrival in Vaikuṇṭha across the Virajā.

stages.name: prāpti
stages.description: Attaining the Lord and eternal service.

name: Parting from the Four Attachments as a path

stages.name: not attached to one's own purpose

notes: Bands approximate (bodhicitta placed in preparatory discipline; the view at first seeing).

name: The five stages of the Pāśupata path (avasthā-pañcaka)

stages.name: vyakta (manifest)
stages.gloss: the stage in which the Pāśupata sign is shown
stages.description: After initiation the brahmin lives in the temple under his teacher, bathes and lies in ash, wears the used garland, worships with laughter, song, dance, the ḍuṇḍuṅ sound, prostration and muttering, keeps the ten restraints and lives on alms. Place: the teacher. Gain: knowledge. Purification: removal of turbidity.
stages.ref: GK 5-7; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 2, 5, 6; PS 1.2-1.17; PABh on PS 5.29

stages.name: avyakta (unmanifest)
stages.gloss: the stage in which sign and learning are hidden
stages.description: With the teacher's leave, having gained knowledge, he goes among people with his sign hidden and courts dishonour by feigned sleep, trembling, limping, amorous gestures, senseless acts and speech, and by wandering like a madman on discarded food; revilers take his demerit and give him their merit. Place: people. Gain: austerity (the whole of dharma).
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5; PS 3.1-4.18; PABh on PS 3.12-17, 5.29

stages.name: jaya (conquest)
stages.gloss: the stage of conquering the senses
stages.description: In an empty house or cave he conquers the senses, recites the chosen Gāyatrī, meditates on Oṃ with fixation in the heart and remains constantly with the god; after six months of constant yoga the powers arise in abundance. Place: cave. Gain: constant union with the god.
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5; PS 5.1-25; PABh on PS 5.13, 5.29

stages.name: cheda (cutting)
stages.gloss: the stage ending in the cutting [of bonds]
stages.description: He lives in the cremation ground until the body falls, on whatever comes, always remembering Rudra; he attains union with Rudra. Place: cremation ground. Gain: steadiness / union.
stages.ref: GK 5-6; Ratnaṭīkā on GK 5, 6; PS 5.30-34; PABh on PS 5.29

stages.name: niṣṭhā (completion)
stages.gloss: the stage in which all activity has ceased
stages.description: All the practitioner's activity has ceased; without body, his place is Rudra alone; having cut the root of the faults and fixed the mind on Rudra, vigilant, he reaches the end of sufferings by the Lord's grace and does not return. Gain: perfection (the Lord's qualities).

notes: Stage names from the Gaṇakārikā; Kauṇḍinya gives the same progression through residence, livelihood, strength, action, purification and gain. Initiation (B0) precedes stage 1. Bands are interpretation-layer claims: the first two stages are ascetic-ritual preparation (B2), conquest of the senses in solitude is withdrawal and concentration (B3, with absorption and powers as it matures), the cremation-ground stage is deepening after the powers (B6), completion is final liberation (B7). The Ratnaṭīkā rejects a separate 'stage of the perfected'.

name: The Prābhākara way to release (Śālikanātha)

stages.name: saṃsāra-udvega
stages.gloss: aversion to the sorrows of saṃsāra
stages.description: Troubled by worldly sorrows and indifferent even to the pleasures mixed with them, one rises for release.

stages.name: niṣiddha-kāmya-nivṛtti

stages.description: Abstaining from the causes of bondage and from means to prosperity.

stages.name: bhoga

stages.name: ātmajñāna with śama, dama, brahmacarya
stages.gloss: self-knowledge supported by calm, restraint, celibacy

stages.name: dehoccheda

stages.name: huishou 回首

stages.name: xunfu 馴伏

stages.name: wuai 無礙

stages.name: renyun 任運

stages.name: xiangwang 相忘

stages.name: duzhao 獨照
stages.description: The herder alone, shining.

stages.name: shuangmin 雙泯
stages.description: An empty circle.

stages.name: savitarka
stages.description: Cultivation on gross elements and senses, mixed with word and meaning; grasped-coalescence.

stages.name: nirvicāra

stages.name: sāsmita
stages.description: Cultivating pure sattva, mere being; those who stop here are 'prakṛtilayas'.

stages.name: viveka-khyāti (grahītṛ-samāpatti)
stages.description: For those who know the supreme puruṣa and continue cultivation.

stages.name: asamprajñāta
stages.description: Rejecting every arising activity 'not this, not this'; only impressions remain.

name: The Rāma Gītā's path from duty to merging (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa 7.5)

stages.name: sva-varṇāśrama-kriyā
stages.gloss: duties of one's class and stage
stages.description: Performing prescribed actions purifies the mind.

stages.name: sad-guru-āśraya
stages.description: Giving up the means already used, one approaches a teacher for self-knowledge.

stages.name: karma-tyāga, ātmānusandhāna
stages.description: Since knowledge and action cannot be combined, the seeker gives up action and inquires.

stages.name: vākyārtha-jñāna
stages.gloss: knowing the meaning of 'that thou art'
stages.description: By faith, the teacher's grace and partial implication the identity is known.

stages.name: samādhi / praṇava-laya
stages.gloss: meditation dissolving A-U-M into the Self
stages.description: Contemplating 'I am light, unborn...' and dissolving the syllables of Oṃ.

stages.name: jīvanmukti

stages.name: mayi pravilaya

stages.name: karmārpaṇa

stages.name: jñāna-miśrā bhakti

stages.name: rādhā-prema
stages.description: Rādhā's love as the crown of all.

stages.name: prema-vilāsa-vivarta

name: The path of the Raseśvara-darśana (body, yoga, liberation in life)

stages.name: gurusevā, dīkṣā
stages.description: The qualified disciple serves and pleases the guru, receives initiation and the secret teaching.

stages.name: rasa-saṃskāra; lohavedha

stages.description: RESTRICTED — summarized only: mercury is purified and processed; its power is first tested on metal.

stages.name: dehavedha; piṇḍasthairya

stages.name: yogābhyāsa (rasa and pavana)
stages.gloss: yoga practice in the stable body
stages.description: Practice of yoga, with breath as the second 'discipline of action'; knowledge arises from practice.

stages.name: cinmaya jyotis
stages.gloss: the conscious light between the brows
stages.description: For some of meritorious vision the conscious light between the eyebrows opens: supreme bliss, free of conception.

stages.name: brahmatva ihaiva
stages.description: Placing the mind there and seeing the world as consciousness, bonds of karma cut, one attains brahmanhood here — liberation in life.

stages.name: jīvanmukta siddhas
stages.description: Freed of passion and hatred, same toward all, they live on in shining bodies, their work done.

name: Higher status and definite goodness (Ratnāvalī)

stages.name: The dharma of higher status
stages.description: Through faith: the ten virtuous paths, non-drinking, right livelihood, non-harm, giving, honouring the honourable and love, leading to happiness in good rebirths.

stages.name: The dharma of definite goodness
stages.description: Through wisdom: seeing that 'I' and 'mine' are false and passing beyond existence and non-existence, which is liberation.

stages.name: The bodhisattva's collections and grounds
stages.description: The collections of merit and wisdom and the ten grounds leading to the two bodies of a Buddha.

stages.name: Buddhahood
stages.description: The form bodies from merit and the truth body from wisdom.

name: The ladder of births to name-recitation (Rudrayāmala, quoted by Bhāskararāya)

stages.name: dīkṣita
stages.gloss: initiated after many births of merit
stages.description: Only after many births of merit is one initiated.

stages.name: śiva-viṣṇu-parāyaṇa
stages.description: By great fortune one becomes devoted to Śiva or Viṣṇu.

stages.name: śakti-bhāva
stages.description: Then the disposition toward Śakti arises.

stages.name: sundarī-bhāva
stages.description: Then by great good fortune the disposition toward Sundarī (Tripurasundarī).

stages.name: turīyā antargatā
stages.description: Then the fourth is reached within.

stages.name: nāma-saṅkīrtana
stages.description: Rarest of all, the singing of her names.

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: In that birth the Goddess, pleased, grants liberation while living; nothing more remains to be done.

notes: Known here through Bhāskararāya's quotation of the Rudrayāmala (checked in the local e-text).

name: Rūpa Gosvāmī's sequence of the arising of love (premṇaḥ prādurbhāve kramaḥ)

stages.name: śraddhā
stages.description: First, faith.

stages.name: sādhu-saṅga
stages.description: Then the company of holy devotees.

stages.name: bhajana-kriyā
stages.description: Then the practice of devotion (the limbs of sādhana-bhakti: hearing, chanting, remembering, service …).

stages.name: anartha-nivṛtti
stages.description: Then what is unwanted falls away.
stages.band_note: B1 by kind (purification), kept in the text's order after practice.

stages.name: niṣṭhā
stages.description: Then steadiness.

stages.name: ruci
stages.description: Then taste (relish) for devotion.

stages.name: āsakti
stages.description: Then attachment.

stages.name: bhāva (rati)
stages.description: Then bhāva: of the nature of special pure sattva, like a ray of the sun of prema, softening the heart; its signs are forbearance, not wasting time, detachment, freedom from pride, hope, longing, taste for the name …

stages.name: prema
stages.description: Then love rises: bhāva become dense, thoroughly softening the heart, marked by an excess of possessiveness toward the Lord.
stages.band_note: B7 as the tradition's final goal (prayojana); the Gauḍīyas deny that prema is the same as mokṣa — they hold it makes liberation trivial (BRS 1.1.17).

equivalents.note: Viśvanātha Cakravartin's Mādhurya-kādambinī expounds the same nine stages (subdividing practice and the anarthas); bands identical.
Continues stage 9: prema → sneha → māna → praṇaya → rāga → anurāga → mahābhāva.
Nārada's aphorisms also lead from renunciation and company of the great to love.

tradition_objection: Prema is the 'fifth goal of life' beyond liberation; Rūpa's tradition rejects any reading of it as merging (sāyujya) and treats desire for liberation as an obstacle ('the witch of desire for enjoyment and liberation', BRS 1.2.22).

stages.name: yoga (saha-mārga)

stages.band_note: Begins at B5 (recognition through the guru); its 'abiding' (niṭṭai) is B6.

stages.name: worship of the devotees and the temple

equivalents.note: The Tamil ten acts (tacakāriyam) articulate the jñāna-pāda's culmination.
Both lead through devotional practice to a relational culmination (union as servant; prema) rather than identity.
Both end in liberation through knowledge given by grace/teaching; the Siddhānta rejects Advaita's identity of soul and Śiva (sāyujya is inseparability, not identity).

tradition_objection: The Siddhānta insists that in liberation the soul neither becomes Śiva nor perishes but abides inseparable from him (Cittiyār cupakkam 11); an equivalence of stage 6 with Advaita's jīvanmukti/videhamukti holds only as 'same band', not same state.
notes: In the Āgamas the four pādas are also the four sections of an Āgama (vidyā/jñāna, kriyā, yoga, caryā). Tirumūlar teaches that each pāda contains the others in miniature (caryā-in-caryā … jñāna-in-jñāna), so the four are not strictly exclusive stages. The first three yield the lower liberations (sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya) and ripen the soul; only jñāna gives sāyujya.

stages.description: After the channels are purified: lightness, radiance, strong digestion, a fragrant and beautiful body; in breath-control sweat (to be rubbed in), trembling, frog-like hopping and rising from the ground; the danger of women's attraction and loss of bindu; repetition of the praṇava against obstacles.

stages.name: ghaṭa
stages.description: Prāṇa and apāna, nāda and bindu, the individual and supreme self join; the retention is lengthened and the senses are withdrawn, whatever is perceived being regarded as the self; powers arise that are to be hidden.

stages.name: paricaya
stages.description: The breath, with the fire, awakens kuṇḍalinī and enters the suṣumnā; the centres are pierced; the yogin sees the 'three peaks' of his karma and destroys them; the five element-concentrations are practised.

stages.name: niṣpatti
stages.description: Samādhi by one's own act; crossing the seeds of beginningless karma one drinks the nectar; the yogin is liberated while living and may leave the body at will or roam the worlds with the powers.

notes: Complements U28's pth:hyp-nada-four-stages (the same four names read through the inner sounds) and U51's pth:hatha-four-stages. Bands are interpretive.

name: The order of the Six Yogas of Nāropa

stages.name: bar do and 'pho ba
stages.gloss: intermediate state and transference — the methods for those who have not reached union in life

notes: Order as in the Karṇatantravajrapada and bka' dpe phyi ma (inner heat → illusory body → dream → clear light → union), with bardo and transference as the fallbacks at death (unbanded). Restricted practices: the map records stages only.

name: The sixteen contemplations of the Contemplation Sūtra

stages.name: the images
stages.description: 'this mind makes the Buddha, this mind is the Buddha'

stages.name: one's own birth in a lotus
upper grades of birth
stages.description: the three minds; three upper grades

stages.name: lower grades of birth
stages.description: ten recitations at death

notes: Contemplations 14-16 describe grades of beings rather than stages of meditation; left unbanded.

name: The sixteen insight knowledges (soḷasa ñāṇa)

stages.name: nāmarūpa-pariccheda-ñāṇa
stages.description: Distinguishing the noted object from the noting mind; mentality and materiality defined, no self apart from them.

stages.name: paccaya-pariggaha-ñāṇa
stages.description: Seeing their conditionality through the three times; doubt overcome.

stages.name: sammasana-ñāṇa
stages.description: Comprehending formations as impermanent, painful, not-self (unpleasant sensations are often prominent — Mahāsi).

stages.name: udayabbaya-ñāṇa
stages.gloss: knowledge of rise and fall (tender, then mature; the ten imperfections arise at its tender stage)
stages.description: Seeing arising and passing; lights, rapture, tranquillity, strong faith may appear and must not be taken for the path.
stages.band_note: Mundane insight: B4 under this unit's rule; U37's pth:pa-auk-path puts mundane insight at B5-B6.

stages.name: bhaṅga-ñāṇa
stages.description: Only the vanishing of formations is seen.

stages.name: bhaya-ñāṇa
stages.description: Formations appear fearful, like a burning house.

stages.name: ādīnava-ñāṇa
stages.description: Formations seen as full of danger.

stages.name: nibbidā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Disenchantment with all formations.

stages.name: muñcitukamyatā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Wish to escape formations, as a man in a burning house seeks the way out.

stages.name: paṭisaṅkhā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Re-observing formations by the three characteristics in order to be freed.

stages.name: saṅkhārupekkhā-ñāṇa
stages.description: Neutral, effortless noting of formations; the three doors of liberation; insight leading to emergence.

stages.name: anuloma-ñāṇa
stages.description: Conforms to the preceding knowledges and to the requisites of awakening.

stages.name: gotrabhū-ñāṇa
stages.description: Passes from the worldling lineage to the noble lineage, taking nibbāna as object.
stages.band_note: Threshold: takes nibbāna as object but is not yet path; banded with the path (B5).

stages.name: magga-ñāṇa
stages.description: The supramundane path abandoning fetters (first path: personality view, doubt, clinging to rules).

stages.name: phala-ñāṇa
stages.description: The fruit immediately following the path.

stages.name: paccavekkhaṇa-ñāṇa
stages.description: Reviewing path, fruit, nibbāna, defilements abandoned and remaining.
stages.band_note: B5 after the first path; for each higher path the series recurs and belongs to B6, ending with arahantship (B7).

equivalents.note: Knowledges 1-2 fall in purifications 3-4, 3-4 in 5, 4-12 in 6, 13-16 around and in 7.
Mahāsi Sayadaw's practical account of the same knowledges through noting.
Sarvāstivāda: heat, peak, patience and supreme mundane quality precede the path of seeing, as mundane insight precedes the path here.

notes: Correction to the unit brief: the count of sixteen is post-canonical — the Visuddhimagga distributes these knowledges over purifications 3-7 and the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha counts ten insight knowledges (comprehension → conformity); the list of sixteen is the later manual count taught in Burma (e.g. by Mahāsi Sayadaw). The Paṭisambhidāmagga's list of seventy-three knowledges is a different scheme.

name: The Vedic ritual career: from initiation to the soma rites and the world of the fathers

stages.name: upanayana
stages.description: The teacher takes the student in as an embryo and imparts the Sāvitrī (AVŚ 11.5.3; RV 3.62.10).

stages.name: brahmacarya and svādhyāya
stages.description: Life with the teacher in fuel, girdle, toil and tapas; learning one's śākhā by recitation (AVŚ 11.5; RV 7.103.5).

stages.name: agnyādhāna
stages.gloss: establishing the fires (as a married householder)
stages.description: The householder and his wife establish the three fires.

stages.name: agnihotra, darśapūrṇamāsa
stages.description: Lifelong daily and new/full-moon offerings.

stages.name: cāturmāsya, paśubandha
stages.description: Seasonal rites (incl. the Tryambaka offerings) and the animal sacrifice.

stages.name: dīkṣā and agniṣṭoma
stages.gloss: consecration and the first soma sacrifice
stages.description: 'Here I go from untruth to truth'; the soma pressed, offered and drunk: 'we have become immortal' (VS 1.5; RV 8.48.3).

stages.name: further soma rites; agnicayana; (for kings) rājasūya, aśvamedha
stages.description: Greater soma rites and the fire altar, opened by the yoking of the mind (VS 11.1–5).

stages.name: pitṛmedha: to Yama and the fathers
stages.description: At death, carried by Agni to the fathers and Yama in the highest heaven, rejoined with iṣṭāpūrta (RV 10.14.8); the ideal before it, a full life of a hundred autumns.

notes: The Saṃhitās do not present a staged liberation path; this is the ritual sequence the śrauta lineages follow (its order is fixed in the sūtras, U02). Bands are interpretive: the final stage is left unbanded because heaven (svarga) is not liberation in the band scale's sense, and the later tradition itself distinguishes them.

name: The seven attentions to the first absorption (Śrāvakabhūmi)

stages.name: lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī manaskāra
stages.description: Discerning the coarseness of sense-pleasures and the peace of the first absorption.

stages.name: ādhimokṣika
stages.description: Resolving on that understanding beyond hearing and reflection.

stages.name: prāvivekya
stages.description: Abandoning the strongest afflictions of the desire realm.

stages.name: ratisaṃgrāhaka
stages.description: Delighting in the abandonment and abandoning the middling afflictions.

stages.name: mīmāṃsā
stages.description: Examining whether desire remains.

stages.name: prayoganiṣṭha
stages.description: Abandoning the subtle afflictions; the preparatory stage completed.

stages.name: prayoganiṣṭhāphala
stages.description: Entering the first absorption proper.

notes: Names checked in the e-text; the functions of stages 2–6 are recalled from the standard explanation.

name: The nine enclosures of the Śrīcakra as a sequence

stages.name: trailokyamohana-cakra (bhūpura)
stages.description: Presiding goddess Tripurā; Prakaṭa yoginīs; the powers Aṇimā etc., the eight Mothers (in the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad the six passions with merit and demerit), the ten mudrā-powers.

stages.name: sarvāśāparipūraka-cakra (16 petals)
stages.description: Tripureśī; Gupta yoginīs; the sixteen attractions (in the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad the elements, senses and mind).

stages.name: sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa-cakra (8 petals)
stages.description: Tripurasundarī; Guptatara yoginīs; the eight Anaṅga goddesses (speech, grasping, going, excreting, bliss, rejecting, accepting, indifference).

stages.name: sarvasaubhāgyadāyaka-cakra (14 triangles)
stages.description: Tripuravāsinī; Sampradāya yoginīs; the fourteen channels.

stages.name: sarvārthasādhaka-cakra (outer 10)
stages.description: Tripurāśrī; Kulottīrṇa yoginīs; the ten vital airs.

stages.name: sarvarakṣākara-cakra (inner 10)
stages.description: Tripuramālinī; Nigarbha yoginīs; the ten fires.

stages.name: sarvarogahara-cakra (8 triangles)
stages.description: Tripurāsiddhā; Rahasya yoginīs; the eight goddesses of speech.

stages.name: sarvasiddhiprada-cakra (triangle)
stages.description: Tripurāmbā; Atirahasya yoginīs; Kāmeśvarī, Vajreśvarī, Bhagamālinī (the unmanifest, mahat, ahaṃkāra).

stages.name: sarvānandamaya-cakra (bindu)
stages.description: Mahātripurasundarī with Kāmeśvara; Parāparātirahasya yoginī; the non-difference of knower, knowing and known.

notes: The texts present the enclosures as the order of worship (from outer to inner); the Bhāvanā Upaniṣad maps them onto body and mind and makes the centre the non-duality of knower and known. Reading the order as stages of attainment, and the bands, are interpretive (low confidence). Names of the cakras and yoginī classes from memory.

name: The way of surrender (Śrīvaiṣṇava prapatti)

stages.name: ācārya-samāśrayaṇa
stages.description: Seeking out a true teacher of the lineage.

stages.name: pañcasaṃskāra
stages.description: Initiation with the marks, name, mantras and instruction in worship.

stages.name: artha-pañcaka and rahasya-traya
stages.gloss: learning the five things and the three secrets
stages.description: Learning the nature of self, Lord, means, goal and obstacle, and the meaning of the three mantras.

stages.name: ākiñcanya and ananyagatitva
stages.description: Knowing oneself to have no means and no other refuge.

stages.name: prapatti
stages.description: Taking refuge at the feet of Nārāyaṇa with Śrī — performed as a means (Vaṭakalai) or accepted as the Lord's being the means (Teṅkalai); after it one has done what is to be done.

stages.name: uttarakṛtya: life of service
stages.description: Service to the Lord and his devotees, recollection of the dvaya, avoidance of offences, duties as command (V) or as service (T).

stages.name: niryāṇa and arcirādi
stages.gloss: departure and the path of light
stages.description: At the end of the body the Lord himself leads the soul out and along the path of light; no last remembrance needed.

stages.name: paripūrṇa-brahmānubhava
stages.description: In Vaikuṇṭha the soul's nature is manifest and it enjoys the Lord fully.

stages.name: nitya-kainkarya
stages.description: Eternal service to the divine couple.

notes: Assembled from Deśika's and Piḷḷai Lokācārya's works; the two schools differ on stage 5 (means or acceptance) and 6 (duties as command or as service). Band B5 for surrender is interpretive: the tradition treats it as the decisive, irreversible act after which liberation is certain.

name: The Śrīvidyā sequence of initiation and worship (Paraśurāma Kalpasūtra)

stages.name: dīkṣā and Bālā
stages.description: Initiation (śāktī, śāmbhavī, māntrī); the guru's pādukā; the Bālā mantra, then the chosen mantra; an initiatory name ending in '-ānandanātha'.

stages.name: gaṇanāyaka-paddhati
stages.description: Removal of obstacles to the worship of the great vidyā.

stages.name: śrīkrama
stages.description: Purifications, the seat, placements (nyāsa), the special water and the visualization of the Goddess's world in the cakra.

stages.name: lalitā-krama
stages.description: Invocation of the Goddess into the bindu, the sixty-four services, the fifteen Nityās.

stages.name: lalitā-navāvaraṇa-pūjā
stages.description: The full worship of the Śrīcakra enclosure by enclosure.

stages.name: śyāmā-krama and vārāhī-krama
stages.description: Worship of Śyāmā (Mantriṇī) and Vārāhī (Daṇḍinī).

stages.name: parā-krama
stages.description: Worship of the supreme Goddess Parā.

stages.name: homa and the common rules
stages.description: Fire rite and the rules common to all worship.

stages.name: kṛtakṛtyatā / jīvanmukti
stages.description: One steadfast in kula who knows and performs all this has accomplished everything; wherever he dies he is liberated while living.

notes: Stages follow the order of the Kalpasūtra's ten sections. Later manuals add further consecrations (e.g. the sixteen-syllable vidyā and pūrṇābhiṣeka) — not recorded here as stages because their sequence was not checked. Bands are interpretive.

name: The fifty-five stages of the Śūraṅgama

stages.name: four additional practices (heat, summit, patience, highest mundane)

notes: Fifty-five = 10 faiths + 10 abodes + 10 practices + 10 dedications + 4 additional practices + 10 grounds + equal awakening; dry wisdom precedes and wondrous awakening follows. From memory (T945 not local).

name: Ten stages of increasing shedding (Tattvārthasūtra 9.45)

stages.name: samyagdṛṣṭi
stages.description: Right view arisen; shedding begins to multiply.

stages.name: śrāvaka
stages.description: Right view with the small vows.

stages.name: virata
stages.description: The ascetic under the great vows.

stages.name: anantaviyojaka
stages.description: The most intense passions are removed.

stages.name: darśanamoha-kṣapaka
stages.description: View-deluding karma destroyed (destructional right view).

stages.name: upaśamaka
stages.description: Conduct-delusion being subsided (ladder of subsidence).

stages.name: upaśāntamoha
stages.description: Delusion wholly subsided (from here one falls back).

stages.name: kṣapaka
stages.description: Conduct-delusion being destroyed (ladder of destruction).

stages.name: kṣīṇamoha
stages.description: Delusion destroyed; the other destructive karmas follow.

stages.name: jina
stages.description: The omniscient conqueror; greatest shedding, leading to liberation.

notes: The Tattvārthasūtra's own ten-stage series, older than (and mappable onto) the fourteen guṇasthānas.

name: Tejobindu: the fifteen limbs

stages.name: yama
stages.description: Sense-restraint by knowledge 'all is Brahman'.

stages.name: niyama
stages.description: Flow of like thoughts.

stages.name: tyāga
stages.description: Abandoning the world-appearance.

stages.name: mauna
stages.description: Silence where words return.

stages.name: deśa
stages.gloss: the solitary place — where all is pervaded
stages.description: The solitary place — where all is pervaded.

stages.name: kāla
stages.description: Time — the partless.

stages.name: āsana
stages.description: The seat where Brahman-contemplation flows.

stages.name: mūlabandha
stages.description: Brahman, root of worlds.

stages.name: dehasāmya
stages.description: Dissolving in the even Brahman.

stages.name: dṛksthiti
stages.description: Seeing the world as Brahman.

stages.name: prāṇasaṃyamana
stages.gloss: stopping modifications by seeing all as Brahman
stages.description: Stopping modifications by seeing all as Brahman.

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: Seeing the Self in objects.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.gloss: holding the mind wherever it goes in Brahman
stages.description: Holding the mind wherever it goes in Brahman.

stages.name: ātmadhyāna
stages.description: 'I am Brahman alone'.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Forgetting of the modification.

checks.note: The inline refs and paraphrased content were checked against the e-text passages read for the teachings. All 2 teachings it rests on exist and were located in the e-text.

name: The ten grounds of the bodhisattva (daśabhūmi) of the Daśabhūmika Sūtra

stages.name: pramuditā
stages.description: Joy at being born into the Tathāgata's family; freed from five fears; ten great vows; giving predominates.
stages.band_note: B5: the first ground is the path of seeing.

stages.name: vimalā
stages.description: The ten wholesome paths of action kept purely even in their subtle forms; morality predominates.

stages.name: prabhākarī
stages.description: Seeing conditioned things as impermanent and burning; the four dhyānas, formless attainments, immeasurables and superknowledges; patience predominates.

stages.name: arciṣmatī
stages.description: The thirty-seven wings of awakening cultivated; views of self burned away; vigour predominates.

stages.name: sudurjayā
stages.description: The four noble truths and two truths understood in all their forms; worldly arts mastered for beings' sake; meditation predominates.

stages.name: abhimukhī
stages.description: Dependent origination examined: 'this triple world is mind only'; the three doors of liberation before him; wisdom predominates.

stages.name: dūraṅgamā
stages.description: Skilful means; entering cessation moment by moment without realizing it; living in the world while beyond it.

stages.name: acalā
stages.description: Acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas; effortless non-conceptual knowledge; roused by the buddhas from resting in peace to remember his vows; vow predominates.
stages.band_note: B6; Candrakīrti and later Tibetan scholastics hold that the afflictive obscurations are exhausted here (an arhat's freedom), while cultivation continues for the knowledge obscurations.

stages.name: sādhumatī
stages.description: Knowing beings' minds and faculties perfectly; teaching with the four analytical knowledges; power predominates.

stages.name: dharmameghā
stages.description: Consecrated by the rays of all buddhas as a great lord of the dharma, he rains the dharma on beings like a cloud; knowledge predominates.
stages.band_note: The band scheme mentions 'dharmamegha as culmination' under B8; the tenth ground's raining of the dharma has the character of activity (B8), but it precedes buddhahood in the sūtra, so it is banded B6, as on U40's pth:madhyamakavatara-ten-grounds.

stages.name: buddha-bhūmi
stages.description: The ground beyond the ten: perfect buddhahood with the three bodies.

equivalents.note: Candrakīrti's Madhyamakāvatāra follows the same ten grounds and perfections; bands identical.
The Lokottaravāda Mahāvastu has a different list of ten grounds (durārohā …).
The Bodhisattvabhūmi's thirteen abodes include the ten grounds within a longer series.
The East Asian fifty-two stages place the ten grounds after the ten faiths, abodes, practices and dedications.
Ground 1 = path of seeing; 2-10 = path of cultivation.

notes: Names as in the Daśabhūmika (Skt.). The Saṃdhinirmocana pairs the ten grounds with ten perfections (six + means, vow, power, knowledge) and adds a buddha-ground; stage 11 is that ground.

name: Kuoan's ten oxherding pictures (Shiniu tu)

stages.name: xun niu 尋牛
stages.description: The herdsman searches through the wild grasses; the preface: the ox has never been lost — by turning his back on awakening he became estranged.

stages.name: jian ji 見跡
stages.description: Through the sūtras and teachings he sees the footprints: the many vessels are all gold, but he has not yet entered the gate.
stages.band_note: B2: understanding through sūtras and teachings, 'not yet entered the gate'.

stages.name: jian niu 見牛
stages.description: Hearing a sound he glimpses the ox itself: it is not elsewhere, it was always there.
stages.band_note: B5: the first glimpse of one's own nature (kenshō).

stages.name: de niu 得牛
stages.description: He seizes it, but it is wild and old habits pull it back; he must use the whip.
stages.band_note: B6: after seeing, old habits still pull the ox back to the grasses.

stages.name: mu niu 牧牛
stages.description: With rope and whip at hand the ox becomes gentle; thoughts arise one after another, but awakening makes them true.

stages.name: qi niu gui jia 騎牛歸家
stages.description: The struggle over, he rides home playing the flute.

stages.name: wang niu cun ren 忘牛存人
stages.description: At home the ox is forgotten; whip and rope lie idle; he sits alone at ease.
stages.band_note: B6: the object gone, the subject still remains.

stages.name: ren niu ju wang 人牛俱忘
stages.description: Whip, rope, person and ox are all empty — an empty circle.
stages.band_note: B7: the empty circle — ordinary and holy both vanish.

stages.name: fan ben huan yuan 返本還源
stages.description: Returning to the source: the rivers flow and the flowers are red of themselves.
stages.band_note: B7: seeing things as they are (the rivers flow, the flowers are red) without striving.

stages.name: ru chan chui shou 入鄽垂手
stages.gloss: entering the marketplace with helping hands
stages.description: Bare-chested and barefoot he enters the marketplace with wine gourd and staff; the withered trees burst into bloom.
stages.band_note: B8: return to the world to benefit others.

sources.ref: pictures 1-10 with verses and Ciyuan's prefaces

equivalents.note: Puming's series ends in the empty circle (Kuoan's 8); Kuoan adds returning to the source and entering the marketplace.
Another Chan map ending in return to the world of distinctions.
Seeing the ox then taming it matches 'sudden awakening, gradual cultivation'.

tradition_objection: The first preface says the ox was never lost: the pictures describe the ending of an estrangement, not the gaining of something new; Chan teachers use them as skilful means (P6), not as a fixed ladder.
notes: Kuoan Shiyuan (廓庵師遠, 12th c., Linji/Yangqi line), with prefaces by Ciyuan; Xuzangjing X1269 (Kuoan's series) is the text used by U42's teachings. Distinguish from Puming's whitening-ox series (pth:puming-ten-oxherding-pictures).

name: Outer self, inner self, supreme self

stages.name: bahirātman
stages.description: Taking the body and external things as oneself (commentators: guṇasthānas 1–3).

stages.name: antarātman
stages.description: Discerning the self as distinct from the body; the means (guṇasthānas 4–12).

stages.name: paramātman
stages.description: The perfected self — embodied omniscient and bodiless Siddha (13–14 and beyond).

notes: Also in Yogīndu, Hemacandra (YŚ 12) and the Adhyātma writers.

name: The three dispositions (paśu, vīra, divya)

stages.name: paśubhāva
stages.description: purity, restraint, solitude, freedom from desire and anger, breath-yoga, reliance on the Vedic path (Rudrayāmala 17.136-140); 'always pure' (Kālīvilāsa 6.10)

stages.name: vīrabhāva
stages.description: the fearless adept of the Kaula rite and cremation ground (restricted)

stages.name: divyabhāva
stages.description: seeing all as divine; proper to the first ages in the Kālīvilāsa

notes: Whether the three are successive stages of one practitioner or fixed temperaments/ages is itself treated differently by the texts (dsp:bhavas-in-kali-yuga). Only the first stage is banded (on the Rudrayāmala's description).

name: The three principal aspects as a path

stages.name: the correct view
stages.description: Dependent arising and emptiness understood together, not alternately.

stages.name: solitude and effort toward the final goal

name: The development of calm through the signs (Visuddhimagga)

stages.name: sīla-visodhana
stages.description: Fourfold purity of virtue; ascetic practices as suitable.

stages.name: paḷibodhupaccheda
stages.description: The ten impediments cut off.

stages.name: kammaṭṭhāna-gahaṇa
stages.description: Approaching the good friend and receiving a subject suited to one's temperament; finding a suitable dwelling.

stages.name: parikamma
stages.gloss: preliminary work with the preliminary sign
stages.description: Attending to the device or object.

stages.name: uggaha-nimitta
stages.description: The image appears with eyes closed as with eyes open.

stages.name: upacāra-samādhi with paṭibhāga-nimitta
stages.gloss: access concentration with the counterpart sign
stages.description: Hindrances suppressed; the purified sign arises and is guarded with the seven suitables.

stages.name: appanā (first jhāna)
stages.description: Through the ten skills, absorption arises; the five masteries are developed.

stages.name: higher jhānas and formless attainments
stages.description: Second to fourth (fifth) jhāna; the four formless states on the kasiṇa basis.

stages.name: abhiññā (optional)
stages.description: The mundane direct knowledges from the fourth jhāna, with the warning that they impede insight.

notes: Bands are interpretation-layer assignments by U37; the preliminary 'taking the subject' is placed in B0 though it comes after virtue in the text's order.

name: The three trainings (tisso sikkhā / triśikṣā): virtue, concentration, wisdom

stages.name: adhisīla-sikkhā
stages.description: Restraint by the Pātimokkha, the monk's virtue (abstaining from killing, stealing, unchastity, false speech …) that brings blameless happiness; right speech, action and livelihood belong here.

stages.name: adhicitta-sikkhā
stages.description: The four jhānas; right effort, mindfulness and concentration belong here; unification of mind is concentration, the four establishments of mindfulness its signs.
stages.band_note: B4 as the jhānas; its preparatory mindfulness and effort are B3.

stages.name: adhipaññā-sikkhā
stages.description: Knowing the four noble truths as they really are; right view and intention belong here.
stages.band_note: B5 as knowing the truths as they are (the path's seeing); its maturing through the higher paths is B6.

stages.name: vimutti
stages.description: The mind imbued with wisdom is rightly freed from the effluents of sensuality, becoming and ignorance.

equivalents.note: The Visuddhimagga expounds its seven purifications within the frame of virtue, concentration and understanding.
The gradual training of DN 2 / MN 27 unfolds the three trainings step by step.
Ethical restraints → concentration → discernment in both; the Yoga Sūtra's goal (isolation of puruṣa) is not the Buddhist liberation.

notes: Pan-Buddhist frame (Pali, Sarvāstivāda, Mahāyāna and Tibetan lamrim all use it). Stage 4 (vimutti) is the fruit named in the recurrent DN 16 talk; the local Pali root text was checked for that quotation.

name: Zhiyi's six identities (liuji 六即)

stages.name: liji 理即
stages.description: One moment of mind is the principle of the tathāgatagarbha — empty, provisional and middle — present in all beings unknowing.
stages.band_note: Starting condition (the ground in all beings), unbanded; Zhiyi's point is that it is already 'identical' with bodhi.

stages.name: mingziji 名字即
stages.description: Hearing from a good friend or the sūtras of the one real bodhi and understanding in words that all dharmas are buddha-dharma; faith in the dharma-nature.

stages.name: guanxingji 觀行即
stages.description: Mind and speech in accord; contemplation unceasing, though not yet in accord with principle (later Tiantai: the five grades of disciples).

stages.name: xiangsiji 相似即
stages.description: The more one contemplates the clearer, like an archer nearing the target; purification of the six senses; ignorance subdued; wisdom resembling the middle way (later: the ten faiths).
stages.band_note: B4: resembling, not yet true, wisdom — the analogue of the path of preparation.

stages.name: fenzhenji 分真即
stages.description: Ignorance first broken, buddha-nature seen, the treasury opened (the abode of arousing the mind), and so on through forty-one stages to equal awakening; manifesting bodies to save beings.
stages.band_note: B5 at its first moment; its further stages up to equal awakening are B6 (with B8 activity: manifesting bodies for beings).

stages.name: jiujingji 究竟即
stages.description: Equal awakening turns into wondrous awakening; wisdom's light complete; the great nirvāṇa, nothing more to cut.

equivalents.note: Zhiyi maps the perfect teaching's stages onto the six identities: resemblance = ten faiths; partial truth = the forty-one stages from the first abode to equal awakening; ultimate = wondrous awakening.
Resemblance ~ preparation; partial truth begins with the first seeing of buddha-nature.

tradition_objection: Zhiyi's point is identity (ji 即): every stage, even the ordinary person's, is identical with bodhi in principle, and the stages exist only to prevent both discouragement and arrogance ('beginning with the ordinary removes doubt; ending with the sage removes arrogance'); he says the six identities are used only for the perfect teaching.
notes: All six names and their explanations verified in the local CBETA text of the Mohe zhiguan (T1911, 10b12-10c24); the text reads 分真即 (partial truth), not the later 分證即. Zhiyi also correlates the Dazhidulun's five bodhis with these stages (10c25ff.).

name: The six stages (ṣaṭsthala) of the Vīraśaiva path

stages.description: One in whom devotion to Śiva has arisen; the dharmas he practises are the bhakta-sthala (initiation, wearing the liṅga, worship of guru, liṅga and jaṅgama); its bhakti is faith; its liṅga the ācāra-liṅga.
stages.band_note: B0 by its bhakti (faith) and entry through liṅga-dīkṣā; its daily worship is B2 in kind.

stages.name: māheśvara
stages.description: Devotion risen to excellence through dispassion; turned away from the stations of Brahmā and the other gods; steadfast in vows and in the liṅga; guru-liṅga.

stages.name: prasādī
stages.gloss: the recipient of grace — with attentiveness (avadhāna)

stages.name: prāṇaliṅgī
stages.gloss: one whose liṅga is the breath — with experience (anubhava)

stages.band_note: B5: first of the three knowledge-predominant sthalas; recognition of the liṅga as consciousness (its inner worship has B4 aspects).

stages.name: śaraṇa

stages.name: aikya
stages.description: Through contemplation of oneness with Śiva, immersion in the great ocean of Śiva's bliss; the self dissolved in the sky of consciousness by equal flavour; mahā-liṅga.

equivalents.note: The 101 sub-sthalas of the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi subdivide these six.
Both ascend by kinds of devotion (faith → steadiness → … → union / prema).

notes: Each sthala is paired with one of six liṅgas (ācāra, guru, śiva, cara/jaṅgama, prasāda, mahā) and six forms of devotion (śraddhā, niṣṭhā, avadhāna, anubhava, ānanda, samarasa; cf. cpt:sadvidha-bhakti). The first three are 'action-predominant', the last three 'knowledge-predominant' (SŚ 12.2-3). The vacanakāras (Basava, Allama, Cennabasava) use the same six stages in Kannada.

name: The seven stages of knowledge (jñāna-bhūmikā) of the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha

stages.name: śubhecchā
stages.description: Preceded by dispassion, the wish: 'why do I remain a fool? I shall look to scripture and the good.'

stages.description: The turn to right conduct through contact with scripture and the good, with dispassion and practice.
stages.band_note: B2 as scripture-based inquiry and practice; it includes the turn to right conduct (B1 in kind).

stages.name: tanumānasā
stages.description: From the first two, non-attachment to sense-objects; desire is thinned.

stages.name: sattvāpatti
stages.description: From practice of these three, the mind rests in pure sattva, the self; Vidyāraṇya calls one here a 'knower of Brahman' (brahmavid).

stages.name: asaṃsakti
stages.description: Detachment from all things through the maturing of the fourth; the knower rises from absorption by himself (brahmavid-vara).

stages.name: padārthābhāvanī
stages.description: Things outside and inside cease to present themselves; he rises from absorption only when roused by others (varīyān).

stages.name: turyagā
stages.description: Abiding in the self alone; this belongs to those liberated while living, who, when prompted, follow customary conduct 'like one half-asleep' (variṣṭha).
stages.band_note: B7 as the attainment of liberation while living; the liberated one's unaffected customary conduct is a B8 facet of the same stage.

stages.name: turyātīta
stages.description: The domain of the bodiless liberated (videhamukta), beyond the seven stages; 'liberation lies beyond the seven'.

equivalents.note: The Varāha Upaniṣad gives the same seven stages (tanumānasī, padārthabhāvanā as variant spellings).
The Mahā Upaniṣad pairs these seven stages of knowledge with seven stages of ignorance.
Vidyāraṇya's Pañcadaśī 7 gives a different sevenfold series of the jīva's states (ignorance → satisfaction).
Graded knowers in the Yoga tradition (the bhāṣya's four kinds of yogin).

notes: Vasiṣṭha himself says the first three stages are 'waking-like' states of the seeker, the fourth dream-like, the fifth deep-sleep-like, the sixth and seventh turya and beyond (Mokṣopāya 6.140-156); Vidyāraṇya's Jīvanmuktiviveka grades the knower as brahmavid (4), brahmavid-vara (5), varīyān (6), variṣṭha (7). Stage 8 (turyātīta) is stated in the same passage and added to reach the text's own end.

stages.name: anālambana
stages.description: Meditation on the formless Siddha, leading to omniscience and the cessation of all yoga.

notes: Each of the five has four grades: desire (icchā), practice (pravṛtti), steadiness (sthira), perfection (siddhi).

name: The three kinds of worship (Yoginīhṛdaya)

stages.name: aparā pūjā
stages.description: Worship of the Śrīcakra and its enclosure deities, done even by Śiva, because it produces the conviction of non-difference.

stages.name: parāparā pūjā
stages.description: Meditative worship dissolving the outer into the inner non-dual abode of consciousness.

stages.name: parā pūjā
stages.description: Abiding in non-duality across every outflow of the senses: 'wherever the mind goes, there is the supreme state'.

notes: The text names the three in the order parā, aparā, parāparā; the ascending order here follows the Dīpikā's grading (aparā lowest, parā highest). Knowing this code makes one liberated while living (YH 3.1).

name: Zongmi's ten phases of awakening (悟十重) in the Chan Preface

stages.name: dunwu 頓悟 (jiewu 解悟)
stages.description: Meeting a good friend, one understands the original enlightened true mind; the four elements are not self, the aggregates empty; faith in one's own suchness and the Three Jewels.
stages.band_note: B5 as the understanding-awakening; the phases after it are all 'cultivation after awakening' (B6).

stages.name: fa beizhi yuan 發悲智願
stages.description: Pledging to realize bodhi.
stages.band_note: B0 in kind (arousing the mind) but placed by Zongmi after awakening, within cultivation (B6).

stages.name: suifen xiuxi 隨分修習
stages.description: Giving, precepts, patience, vigour and calming-and-contemplation; the root of faith grows.
stages.band_note: B1-B3 in kind; after awakening (B6).

stages.name: da putixin xianfa 大菩提心顯發
stages.gloss: the great mind of awakening manifests
stages.description: The great bodhicitta becomes manifest.

stages.name: zhi faxing 知法性
stages.description: Knowing the dharma-nature to be free of stinginess and the rest.
stages.band_note: Phases 5 and 6 are not clearly separated in the digital rendering of the chart.

stages.name: suishun xiu liudu, wofa shuangwang 隨順修六度 我法雙亡
stages.gloss: the perfections in accord; self and dharmas both forgotten
stages.description: Practising the six perfections in accord with the dharma-nature; by samādhi and prajñā self and dharmas are forgotten — always empty, always illusory.

stages.name: yu se zizai 於色自在
stages.description: All interfused.

stages.name: yu xin zizai 於心自在
stages.description: Illuminating everything.

stages.name: jiujing jue 究竟覺
stages.description: Means fulfilled, one thought in accord; the first arising of mind awakened, free of subtle thought.

stages.name: da jue zun 大覺尊
stages.description: No separate initial awakening; one with the pure mind-source, responding in countless ways and abiding in the dharma-realm; seeing all beings as equally awakened.
stages.band_note: B7, with the B8 aspect of responsive activity (應用塵沙).

equivalents.note: Jinul condenses Zongmi's sequence into sudden awakening, gradual cultivation and realization.

notes: Zongmi pairs ten phases of delusion (from the original enlightened mind, through non-awakening, to the reception of karmic results) with ten phases of awakening that overturn them in reverse order. The phase names used here are descriptive labels drawn from the chart's text as read in CBETA (T2015); they are not a fixed list of titles, and the division of phases 5-6 is uncertain.
